Amazon's early Black Friday 2026 sale is already bringing substantial discounts to smart TVs, with savings ranging from $200 to $1,350 across models from Samsung, LG, Hisense, Sony, TCL, and other major brands. Several of the TVs included are from this year's lineups, so you don't necessarily have to settle for an older model to get a good price. There's also a decent variety to choose from, whether you're looking for an OLED TV with excellent contrast for movie nights, a bright mini-LED display for a sunlit living room, or simply a bigger screen without spending a fortune.

We've rounded up some of the more interesting offers below, and you can check out the rest of our Black Friday coverage for more editor-vetted tech deals as the sale continues.

Samsung’s 65-inch S90H is down to $1,397.99 from $1,897.99, saving you $500 on the company’s mid-range OLED TV for 2026. It’s a solid option for movie enthusiasts and gamers alike, thanks to its self-lit pixels that produce deep blacks and excellent contrast, particularly in darker scenes where conventional LED TVs can struggle with a grayish glow. You also get a high-refresh-rate display for smoother gaming.

If you have room for a bigger screen, Samsung’s 77-inch S85H is also worth a look, especially now that it’s down to $1,797.99 from $2,197.99, saving you $400. Although it sits below the S90H in Samsung’s 2026 OLED lineup, it still delivers the deep blacks, excellent contrast, and wide viewing angles that make OLED TVs appealing. The larger screen also makes it a good fit for family movie nights.

One of the biggest discounts in this roundup, the 2026 75-inch Hisense U7 is now $997.99, down from $1,999.99. Its mini-LED backlighting and local dimming are designed to deliver brighter highlights and better contrast, making it an appealing option for rooms with plenty of natural light. Gaming-focused features also make it worth a look if you plan to connect a current-generation console or gaming PC.

For a more affordable 75-inch option, Hisense's 2026 U6 Pro is down to $699.99 from $1,399.99, saving you $700. Like the U7, it uses mini-LED backlighting to improve contrast and bring out more detail in HDR movies and shows, although it sits a tier below the U7 in terms of overall picture performance. It also comes with Fire TV and Alexa+ built in, making it a convenient choice for households already using Amazon's smart home ecosystem.

The C6 is LG’s mid-range OLED evo model for 2026, and right now its 65-inch model is $1,399.99, down from its $2,699.99 launch price. It combines excellent pixel-level contrast with gaming features designed for fast-paced titles, making it a versatile choice for both movies and consoles. LG also supports Dolby Vision, which gives it an advantage over Samsung's OLEDs for viewers who regularly stream compatible HDR content.

Sony’s 65-inch Bravia 6, the entry-level OLED in its 2026 TV lineup, is now $1,198, down from $1,999.99, saving you $802. It delivers the deep blacks and excellent contrast you'd expect from the display technology, thanks to its self-lit pixels. Sony's picture processing also helps bring out fine details and natural-looking colors in movies and TV shows, while Dolby Vision support makes the most of compatible HDR content.

For the same $1,198, you can get a considerably larger screen with the 85-inch Sony Bravia 3 II, which is down from $1,599.99, saving you $402. That said, this 2026 model uses a conventional LED panel, so it won't quite match the Bravia 6's deep blacks and contrast, but the extra 20 inches make it an appealing option for sports and family movie nights. It also has a native 120Hz refresh rate with VRR and ALLM for smoother console gaming, along with Dolby Vision support and Google TV with Gemini built in.

Toshiba’s 75-inch Z670R is down to $699.99 from $1,299.99, saving you $600 on a 2026 mini-LED TV. It combines full-array local dimming with QLED color technology for improved contrast and brighter highlights, while Toshiba’s REGZA Engine ZRi processor helps sharpen lower-resolution content. The native 144Hz refresh rate also makes it a good option for console and PC gaming, and you get Fire TV built in for streaming, along with Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos support.

Designed to compete with Samsung's The Frame, Toshiba's 65-inch G700 ArtVision is currently $899.99 at Amazon, down from $1,297.99, saving you $398. It's a 4K QLED TV, with a native 165Hz refresh rate, built-in Fire TV, and the same REGZA Engine ZRi processor found in the Z670R. But there's more to it than watching movies and shows, as its Ambient Mode can display over 3,000 curated artworks without a subscription, while the matte anti-glare screen and included white oak frame help it pass for a framed print on the wall.

TCL’s 98-inch F8D is down to $1,444.99 from $1,699.99, saving you $255 on a massive 2026 QLED Fire TV. It uses a high-brightness LED backlight, so you won't get the same level of contrast control as TCL's more expensive mini-LED QM models, but it still offers a native 144Hz refresh rate for smoother gaming, along with Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos support. And at nearly 100 inches, there's plenty of screen space to make movies, sports, and games feel more immersive.

TCL’s 75-inch QM64L is down to $699.99 after a $200 price cut—it’s the cheapest way into TCL’s 2026 QD-Mini LED lineup, and it pairs quantum dot color with local dimming for brighter highlights and better contrast in HDR movies and sports. That also makes it a good pick for a bright living room, where an OLED might not be the most practical choice. You also get a native 144Hz refresh rate for gaming and Fire TV built in

Roku’s 65-inch Plus Series is the most affordable TV in this roundup at $449.99, down from $649.99, saving you $200. LG’s 65-inch C6 OLED has the largest dollar discount in this sale at $1,350 off, which brings it from $2,699.99 down to $1,349.99.

For a large screen at a relatively affordable price, the 75-inch Hisense U6 Pro at $699.99 stands out, while the 65-inch Roku Plus Series at $449.99 makes sense for everyday streaming on a tighter budget. #3231. The Dynamo-Electric Principle: 160 Years of Powering Industry

How a breakthrough in electromechanical energy conversion helped shape the motors and generators that drive modern industry

Innomotics is a global leader in electric motors and large drive systems, operating from its headquarters in Nuremberg, Germany.

The dynamo-electric principle: one idea, 160 years, millions of motors.

This article is brought to you by Innomotics.

In the annals of industrial history, few innovations have demonstrated such remarkable staying power as the dynamo-electric principle. Discovered by Werner von Siemens in 1866, this groundbreaking principle remains fundamental to modern electrical engineering more than a century and a half later – and continues to shape the technology portfolio of Innomotics, a globally leading provider of electric motors and large drive systems. What began as a breakthrough in electromechanical energy conversion has evolved into a cornerstone of global industry – powering everything from brewery operations in Qingdao to high-voltage drive systems in petrochemical plants.

The year 1866 marked a decisive turning point, not only in the broader arc of industrial transformation but specifically in the realm of electric motion. At a time when Europe was entering a new phase of industrial transformation, Werner von Siemens pioneered the dynamo-electric principle – a breakthrough that enabled electric machines to generate their own magnetic field through self-excitation. This innovation transformed electric machines from laboratory curiosities into practical power sources, enabling the widespread electrification of industry and infrastructure that defined the late 19th century.

This electric motor from Innomotics was installed in the early 1900s at the historic Tsingtao Brewery in China and supported production processes for more than 90 years, operating continuously under industrial conditions.Innomotics

The principle itself is elegantly simple: an iron core generates a stable magnetic field; a rotating coil is placed within this field; movement in the magnetic field induces an electric current; part of this current strengthens the magnetic field; and electrical energy is continuously converted into motion. This self-reinforcing cycle made efficient and reliable electric motion possible – and it remains the foundation of modern motors today.

More than 160 years later, the same fundamental idea continues to power industrial applications around the world. Millions of motors operate reliably under demanding conditions, keeping production running across generations. The dynamo-electric principle made it possible for electric machines to convert electrical energy into motion (and motion back into electrical energy), creating the technological foundation for modern electric motors and drive systems.

Active Vibration Control System (AVCS) enhances stability and reliability by actively reducing vibrations.Innomotics

Perhaps no example illustrates this longevity better than the electric motor from Innomotics at the historic Tsingtao Brewery in China. Installed in the early 1900s during the early electrification of industrial brewing, this motor supported production processes for more than 90 years, operating continuously under industrial conditions. It became a powerful example of long-term reliability in real-world applications – a testament to how engineering ensures reliable motion across decades.

Continuity, however, does not mean stagnation. Sixteen decades after the original breakthrough, innovations continue to emerge that build upon this proven foundation. Two recent developments – the Active Vibration Control System (AVCS) and oil-lubricated rolling bearings (OLRB) – carry this spirit of innovation and ingenuity forward, a commitment that has been recognized with the German Innovation Award.

Innomotics’ patented Oil-Lubricated Rolling Bearing (OLRB) technology enhances reliability and reduces maintenance requirements.Innomotics

AVCS helps optimize high-voltage motor performance by actively decoupling motors from their foundations to reduce vibration issues. OLRB helps prevent rolling bearing failures from the start with continuous lubrication, supporting higher availability, less downtime, and long-term cost savings. These innovations demonstrate how the basic principle of 1866 can be enhanced through modern engineering to meet contemporary demands for reliability and efficiency.

For three decades, with over 25,000 units driving performance globally, Innomotics’ Perfect Harmony GH180 medium-voltage drive platform has supported reliable operation across industries. Its modular architecture enables efficient power control, high availability, and long-term performance. With thousands of installations worldwide, Perfect Harmony GH180 continues to build on a proven technological foundation, minimizing downtime and ensuring stable production.

Keeping critical motors running requires the right expertise and innovation spirit throughout the entire lifecycle. With Innomotics Customer Services, operators and plant managers gain the insights they need to maintain reliability and optimize maintenance strategies. Winding Lifetime Analysis (WLA) combines operating history, machine measurements, and physics-based modeling to assess the condition of the winding insulation and estimate its remaining useful lifetime. This enables informed maintenance decisions, reduces uncertainty, and helps minimize the risk of unplanned downtime.

The Perfect Harmony GH180 delivers efficient, reliable and flexible medium-voltage drive performance.Innomotics

What began as a breakthrough in 1866 still brings its value to modern industry. The dynamo-electric principle made efficient and reliable electric motion possible – and it remains the foundation of modern motors today.

As industries worldwide grapple with challenges ranging from energy efficiency to operational resilience, this 160-year-old principle continues to prove its relevance.

For plant managers and engineers seeking long-term performance in demanding applications, the message is clear: the foundation laid in the 19th century remains as solid as ever. What has changed are the tools and services built upon it – from vibration control systems to predictive analytics – all designed to extract maximum value from a principle that has, quite literally, powered the modern world for a century and a half.

Innomotics, carrying forward a legacy that spans the full arc of this history, continues to move industry forward with innovations that create real progress. The dynamo-electric principle may be 160 years old, but as the company’s portfolio demonstrates, it is far from obsolete. It is, in every sense of the word, still running.

#3230. Apple’s leadership overhaul continues with new Apple Pay and Wallet chief

Bloomberg reports that Apple lifer Corey Fugman will replace Jennifer Bailey as the head of the Apple Pay and Wallet division. Here are the details.

A few months ago, Bloomberg reported that Jennifer Bailey, Apple’s head of Apple Pay and Wallet, who had led Apple Pay since its launch in 2014, would retire in October.

At the time, Apple’s services boss Eddy Cue said internally that the company would announce its succession plan before her transition at the end of October, and that she would “continue to be available to support the transition in an advisory role.”

October came and went without any public announcement on that front. Today, however, Bloomberg reported that Apple has tapped Corey Fugman, “a 26-year company veteran as the new head of its payment service and digital wallet unit.”

According to his LinkedIn profile, Fugman joined Apple in September 2000 as Merchandising Manager for Apple Retail and has held several leadership positions since then, including overseeing Apple Card and Apple Cash from 2019 to 2021.

Most recently, he served as Senior Director of Apple Pay and Wallet, a position he has held since November 2021.

With the new job, Fugman inherits a crucial tap-to-pay business, which is estimated to generate billions of dollars a year. It handles tens of billions of transactions annually across more than 90 markets, with Apple taking a percentage.

The division also includes the Apple Card, which is transitioning from a partnership with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. to JPMorgan Chase & Co. Fugman has been highly involved with the shift to Chase, which is still ongoing, the people said.

The report notes that Fugman will report to Cue, and reaffirms that Bailey “will remain a consultant in the coming months,” echoing Cue’s earlier comments about her role in the transition.

Finally, Bloomberg adds that while Apple has undergone several leadership changes in recent months, including John Ternus replacing Tim Cook as CEO, Cue’s responsibilities have expanded considerably.

In addition to overseeing services such as Apple TV, Apple Music, Maps, and iCloud, Cue has recently taken charge of the App Store and Health following Jeff Williams’ departure as Chief Operating Officer and Phil Schiller’s decision to step down from overseeing the App Store.

#3229. New ‘Friday The 13th’ Movie Unveils Cast, Title & Release Date

EXCLUSIVE: We recently announced the first Friday the 13th film in nearly two decades — and now, we have new details on the project, which wraps production today.

The film, directed by the previously announced Steve Miner, is titled Jason. It’s slated for a worldwide theatrical release on Friday, August 13, 2027, with Cineverse overseeing its North American distribution.

The ensemble cast is led by Schuyler White (Haunt) as Jason Voorhees, the enigmatic masked murderer at the heart of the slasher series, and Natalie Alyn Lind (Dutton Ranch) as “final girl” Lauren.

Others in the cast include Matt Cornett (Every Year After) as Asher, Lilia Buckingham (Hocus Pocus 2) as Madison, John Owen Lowe (Unstable) as Jake, Summer Madison (The Summer I Turned Pretty) as Emily, Selena Turner (Will Trent) as Olive, Matthew Keoni Sato (High School Musical: The Musical: The Series) as Lucas, Brook Sill (Stranger Things) as Zoe, Guillermo Diaz (Scandal) as Rick, Johnell Young (Wu-Tang: An American Saga) as Frank, Sencere Messiah Brown (Homage) as Chase and Bryan Gael Guzman (Nickel Boys) as Dylan. Watch on Deadline

White, a stunt coordinator and special effects artist, returns to the role of Jason after playing him in the recent short Sweet Revenge made to commemorate the 45th anniversary of Jason Universe.

On the decision to cast him here, franchise steward Robbie Barsamian told us, “We spent months thinking about how to create the scariest, most imposing Jason and who truly deserved to wear the mask. Beyond his towering physical presence, we knew Schuyler understood what makes Jason tick—and that he had the work ethic and genuine respect for this franchise to get it right. He approached this theatrical feature like the role of a lifetime, packing 30 pounds of solid muscle onto his 6’5″ frame and studying the iconic Jasons who came before him so that he feels like an unstoppable force of nature. On set, we framed him low and tight, so the audience is right there in his space, looking up at him. This will be the most intimidating Jason that has ever been on screen.”

On casting Lind — an actress seen on Dutton Ranch, The Goldbergs and Big Sky — as the franchise’s new final girl, Barsamian said, “Natalie is not only an excellent actress and incredibly hardworking, but also one of the biggest horror enthusiasts and fans of this franchise. When you put all that together you get something special. This franchise has had many strong female leads, but her performance might just be the strongest this franchise has ever had.”

Jason marks the 13th entry of Friday the 13th, an iconic horror franchise that launched with a namesake 1980 slasher. Working from a script by emerging screenwriter David Fliegel, Miner returned to the director’s chair after introducing Jason’s machete in Friday the 13th Part II and unveiling his hockey mask for the first time in Friday the 13th Part III. The film was made independently to afford the Barsamian family, which financed and produced and control the franchise through their company Horror, Inc., total creative control.

Directed by Sean S. Cunningham, the original Friday the 13th watches as a group of counselors at Camp Crystal Lake, preparing to reopen the summer camp, are stalked and killed by an unseen assailant, while the memory of a boy who drowned there years earlier hangs over the grounds. Produced independently for roughly $550,000 and acquired by Paramount in a bidding war, the film provided the foundation for a durable, low-budget sequel machine, with Paramount releasing early entries and and Warner Bros./New Line joining as distributor from the ’90s on. The original film surprised with the revelation of (SPOILER) matriarch Pamela Voorhees as the murderous antagonist, while later entries embraced the machete-wielding Jason himself as the franchise’s terrifying driving force.

Over the decades, Friday the 13th has spawned video games, immersive experiences, comic books, collectibles, apparel and more, alongside the films. Horror, Inc. launched the Jason Universe to usher in a new era of expansion in the franchise in 2024, and most recently, the franchise has been back in circulation via Crystal Lake, Peacock and A24’s prequel series, which premiered all eight episodes on Oct. 15.

White is repped by Brand in Motion; Lind by CAA, Authentic and Brecheen Feldman Breimer; Cornett by Gersh, LBI Entertainment and Walter Entertainment & Media Law; Buckingham by Buchwald and Industry Entertainment; Lowe by UTA, Untitled and Latham & Watkins; Madison by Formation Talent Agency, Kevin Donahue Management and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller; Turner by Paradigm, Play Management and Forward Talent; Sato by Buchwald and Skrzyniarz & Mallean; Sill by Griffin Talent and Luber Roklin Entertainment; Diaz by Innovative; Young by Eris Talent Agency, Stride Management and Nelson Davis; Brown by Avenue Agency; and Guzman by Formation Talent.

#3228. New iPhone Duo orders now deliver a month earlier than before

Interested in getting an iPhone Duo before Christmas? You might be in luck, as Apple’s online store delivery estimates just got pulled forward by a full month, with December delivery now expected.

Apple seems to be finding success in ramping up its iPhone Duo production.

Within minutes of iPhone Duo pre-orders opening on October 16, delivery estimates quickly slipped into November, then December, and after about a half hour of orders, the earliest you could get an iPhone Duo was late January.

Apple did deliver some Duo units earlier than the initial estimates. But the late January timeframe remained in place for all new iPhone Duo orders until now.

But as spotted by Max Weinbach, new iPhone Duo orders from Apple just got bumped up by about a month. Now, delivery estimates are showing December 16-23 for customers in the US and elsewhere.

New Duo orders seemed to have been pulled forward ~a month They must be scaling manufacturing quickly pic.twitter.com/VFkCmCoRLF

This is a great indicator that Apple has been able to accelerate production. It’s also likely that there was a slowdown in orders due to the late January estimate putting off prospective buyers, thus making it easier for the company to catch up on backorders.

While we still don’t know sales numbers, the iPhone Duo by all appearances has been a hit already. And with iOS 27.3 adding a face unlock feature soon, one of the biggest critiques reviewers had is largely being mitigated.

As PCMag mentions in their review, their sound profile leans warm and bass-forward, with deep lows that suit bass-heavy genres, while the companion app adds Bose Immersive Audio for spatial sound and lets you create customized listening profiles—the three-band EQ is fairly basic, though, so anyone who likes fine-tuning their sound may find the adjustment options limiting.

The Sony WH-1000XM6 came out in 2025 and are the best over-ear headphones I tested last year (or ever, really). These headphones go with a companion app that's packed with a lot more features that you can nerd out on. The audio quality is second to none, with the fully customizable EQ giving you plenty of options to get the sound how you like it. Right now, you can get the WH-1000XM6 headphones for $378 (originally $459.99), their lowest price ever.

Samsung’s 32-inch Odyssey G5 (G51F) gaming monitor has dropped to $179.99 on Amazon, which is the lowest price it has reached so far. It’s a flat panel (unlike Samsung’s many curved gaming displays), with a matte coating that helps minimize glare in brighter rooms, and comes with a stand that supports height, tilt, and pivot adjustments. The G51F’s combination of 180Hz refresh rate, 1ms response time, and AMD FreeSync support makes fast-paced games look smoother and feel more responsive than they do on standard 60Hz displays, especially in shooters, racing games, and competitive multiplayer titles.

If you're interested in the new M5 MacBook, Amazon is the only major retailer offering a $250 discount. The 15-inch MacBook Air is $1,249.99 (originally $1,499), and the new M5 chip is powerful enough to likely carry all of your workload without hiccups.

Budget TVs have improved dramatically over the years, and the Hisense U6 Series is a great example of what you can get today for a "budget" price. This is a QLED Mini LED TV, so while it's not at the quality that OLED TVs can offer, it makes up for it with a much lower price. Right now, the 65-inch Hisense Class U6 Series TV is $529.99 (originally $1,099.99), the lowest price it has been. Don't let the budget price fool you; this is a quality TV. The best one of 2025, according to PCMag's "outstanding" review. Its main attributes are its incredible levels of brightness, peaking at 1,024 nits, and its beautiful colors. This is expected from a QLED Mini LED TV, but not for under $550 for a 65-inch TV. It is also packed with features and specs that you won't find in other TVs at this price.

Right now, the 65-inch QM8L is $997.99 (originally $2,499.99), its lowest price since it launched in April. The QM8L has a “Zero Border” bezel design, which gives it a modern, minimalistic look. When you turn it on, you'll likely note how bright this TV gets. TCL claims it reaches 6,000 nits; no OLED can come close to this unit's brightness. Another important spec to note here is the local dimming zones: TCL claims this TV has up to 4,000, which means it gets top-tier backlight control, limited light blooming, and contrast levels that some might not be able to distinguish from an OLED.

The Hisense E7SF QLED is in the low to mid-range of the OLED category, but with its 45% discount, the price is much lower. Amazon currently has the 65-inch E7SF QLED for $499.99 (originally $999.99), which is especially notable given this model came out in April of this year. The first thing you'll notice about the Hisense E7 is how thin and lightweight it is. It comes with four HDMI connections, one of which is an eARC connection so you can plug in a soundbar, and two with a native 144Hz refresh rate in game mode.

#3224. Apple expands Apple Intelligence beta testing in China to iPads and Macs

Following the arrival of Apple Intelligence on iPhones in China with iOS 27.3 beta 1, Apple is now expanding support to iPads and Macs ahead of the public release of its 27.3 updates. Here are the details.

Apple’s road to releasing Apple Intelligence in China has been a particularly eventful one.

After a significant amount of regulatory back-and-forth, the company confirmed in late October that Apple Intelligence would make its way to iPhones as of iOS 27.3, beginning with the first beta of the system, released in early November.

Just a few days later, Reuters reported that Apple had cleared another regulatory hurdle in the country by registering Apple Intelligence for use on tablets and laptops.

Today, Apple released the second developer betas of iPadOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3, both of which now include Apple Intelligence support in China, as spotted by MacRumors.

As with the initial iPhone rollout in the first iOS 27.3 beta, Apple Intelligence on iPads and Macs in China does not include Siri AI or the other next-generation AI features announced at WWDC 2026.

Instead, users get access to earlier capabilities such as Writing Tools, Genmoji, Live Translation, and notification summaries, with Alibaba’s Qwen model powering certain features.

You can learn more about the Apple Intelligence features set to be available in China at launch here.

EXCLUSIVE: Vin Diesel is stepping outside the Fast & The Furious and Guardians Of The Galaxy franchises to make original action movie Burial Hill, we can reveal.

Diesel is teaming up on the project with Mike McGrale, writer on upcoming John Wick spinoff Caine, and director Jamie Payne, known for directing both of Netflix’s Luther movies and on the original Idris Elba series, as well as on shows including Outlander, The Alienist and Doctor Who.

#3221. ‘Schmigadoon!’ and ‘Widow’s Bay’ land Apple TV two Grammy nominations

Apple TV today celebrated two Grammy nominations, one of which further establishes a canceled show as an unlikely awards success story. Here are the details.

Earlier this year, the Broadway adaptation of Apple TV’s ‘Schmigadoon!’ won four Tony Awards, including Best Musical, making Apple TV an EGOT winner by completing its collection of Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony awards.

‘Schmigadoon!’ premiered on Apple TV in 2021 and ran for two seasons, ending in 2023. In January 2024, show creator Cinco Paul confirmed that, although the third season had already been written with 25 new songs, Apple decided not to move forward with it.

Even before the Broadway adaptation’s Tony wins in June, a May report had raised hopes for the show’s return, revisiting an earlier interview in which ‘Schmigadoon!’ creator Cinco Paul revealed that there had been discussions about reviving it.

While there have been no further updates on a potential revival since then, fans got another reason to celebrate today, as the Broadway cast recording of ‘Schmigadoon!’ has been nominated for Best Musical Theater Album at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

It will compete against CHESS the Musical, The Lost Boys, Ragtime, and Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York).

Additionally, ‘Widow’s Bay‘ earned a nomination for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media, putting composer David Fleming up against the soundtracks of ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘One Battle After Another,’ ‘Project Hail Mary,’ and ‘Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu‘.

The 2027 Grammy Awards will take place on Sunday, February 7, 2027. To check out the full list of nominees, follow this link.

Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month or as part of the Apple One bundle. It features hit TV shows and movies like Ted Lasso, Severance, The Studio, The Morning Show, Shrinking, and Silo.

Becca Lewis is home maintenance writer who aims to foster confidence in and inspire DIY enthusiasts at all skill levels.

If you have a DIY enthusiast on your list—or if you just want some new tools for your own projects—Black Friday sales are a good time to snag low prices on quality tools. Lots of big box stores are looking to thin out their inventory and make room for next year’s upgrades, so in addition to encouraging a holiday rush, retailers are motivated to price things to move. If you know what to look for, you can get up to 65% off on trusted brands. Here are a few of the best deals out there right now.

If you’re building a new cordless tool set, or updating your battery system, getting a cordless tool set can save you some money because these combos usually include batteries and a charger, which can be the most expensive part of your tool set. Here are a few of the best early Black Friday deals on cordless tool sets.

The Ryobi 6-tool 18-volt combo set is on sale for $199, 33% off its regular price at Home Depot. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, a circular saw, a sawzall, an oscillating multi-tool, a work light, a 1.5-amp-hour battery, a 4-amp-hour battery, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a good deal on a trusted home tool brand.

The Ryobi 18-volt drill and driver set is on sale for $99, 34% off its usual price at Home Depot. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, two 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a great starter set because it has the first two tools you need for a cordless kit and it comes with batteries so you can expand your set for cheaper as you develop your skills.

The Ryobi 4-tool, 4-volt project set is on sale for $99, 61% off its typical price at Home Depot. This set comes with a rotary tool, a project light, a glue pen, a mini drill, two rechargeable batteries, a charging cable, a set of starter rotary bits, and three glue sticks. This set is handy for DIY projects that require fine detail, like wood carving, craft projects, or framing pictures.

The DeWalt drill and driver combo set is on sale for $149, 38% off its regular price on Amazon. This set includes a drill, an impact driver, 2 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a good deal on a trusted brand for drills and drivers, and a good start for a cordless DIY tool set.

If you have a cordless tool set already and you want to expand your kit, or if you have a DIYer in your life who already has a particular brand of battery and you want to get them something they can use, a single tool deal can be just the thing.

The DeWalt cordless 20-volt cutout saw is on sale on Amazon for $102.95, 53% off its typical price. This is a tool-only deal, so you’ll need a 20-volt DeWalt battery and charger to use it. This is a good tool for custom trimming drywall, cutting custom shapes for going around outlet covers, or custom cutting trim in tight spaces.

The DeWalt 20-volt cordless angle grinder is on sale at Lowe’s for $209, 47% off its usual price. This tool comes with a 2-amp-hour battery and a 4-amp-hour battery, but you’ll need a DeWalt 20-volt charger to use it. This is a good tool for metalworking or for grinding down screw tips that poke through or trimming bolt ends off.

The DeWalt 20-volt compact drill/driver is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 45% off its usual price. This tool comes with a 20-volt, 2-amp-hour battery and a charger, so it’s ready to use out of the box. It’s a good first tool for a set.

The Milwaukee 18-volt impact wrench is on sale at Home Depot for $199, 68% off its typical price. This tool comes with two 5-amp-hour batteries and a charger, so it’s ready to use out of the box. This is a good tool for driving bolts through tough materials and for automotive projects.

The DeWalt 20-volt oscillating multi-tool is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 50% off its regular price. This tool comes with a 2-amp-hour battery and a charger, so it's ready to use out of the box. This is one of the most versatile cordless tools, allowing you to cut a wide range of materials and use a sanding attachment to do finishing work as well.

The Milwaukee 18-volt tire inflator kit is on sale at Home Depot for $199, 65% off its usual price. This tool comes with two 5-amp-hour batteries and a charger, so it’s ready to go right out of the box. This is an excellent addition to your emergency roadside tool set because you can use it to inflate a car tire with the charged 18-volt batteries.

The Makita 18-volt cordless electric 2-inch brad nailer is on sale on Amazon for $324, 38% off its regular price. This is a tool-only deal, so you’ll need a Makita 18-volt battery and charger to use it. This is a good tool for attaching trim or paneling.

Yes, Home Depot has already launched its early Black Friday deals, offering deep discounts on major brands of cordless power tools. They also update their sales page on Thanksgiving Day and include Black Friday in-store-only doorbusters as part of their seasonal sales.

For most home tool sets, Ryobi is a solid, durable, and versatile brand. If you plan to use your tools occasionally for home maintenance, this is the best bang for your buck. For daily use or for larger DIY projects, DeWalt tends to be the next best option. These tools have more robust chargers and tend to stand up to more rigorous use than Ryobi tools.

If you’re building a new cordless tool set or updating your battery system, getting a cordless tool set can save you money because these combos usually include batteries and a charger, which can be the most expensive part of your tool set. If you already have a cordless tool set and you want to expand your kit, or if you have a DIYer in your life who already has a particular brand of battery and you want to get them something else they can use, a single tool deal might make more sense.

3 shows to watch after you finish binge-watching 'The Body'

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's only been a week since "The Body" came out on Netflix, but the Quinn Shephard psychological horror series has already made its mark, hitting the No. 1 spot on Netflix's Top 10 TV shows chart in the United States and worldwide.

The eight-episode coming-of-age series focuses on a group of 2004-era Catholic school girls (played by Kristina Bogic, Sara Boustany, Geena Meszaros, Sofia Wylie, and Shirley Chen, among others) who trigger mass hysteria in their conservative town after a drug-fueled Halloween night initiation ritual goes wrong.

The show's mix of psychological horror, religious satire and campy eroticism has clearly been a hit with viewers and critics alike (as of press time, it has an 86% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes). And if you want that kind of spooky fun to continue, here are three shows like "The Body" to watch next.

If you haven't yet been stung by the survival horror and dark humor of "Yellowjackets," now's a great time to catch up with the Showtime thriller. Not only does the series feature a similar mix of supernatural eeriness, schoolgirl drama, mass hysteria, and moral murkiness as "The Body," but "Yellowjackets" is also officially entering its fourth and final chapter beginning on November 20.

In case you haven't tuned in yet, the survival saga centers on a high school girls' soccer team as they try to survive in the remote Canadian wilderness after their plane crashes, following the group through two timelines: directly after the crash in 1996, and 25 years later, with the now-adult survivors attempting to reckon with dark secrets and unresolved trauma. That split timeline means we get an iconic cast of both industry vets—including Melanie Lynskey, Juliette Lewis, and Christina Ricci—and notable newcomers like Sophie Nélisse, Jasmin Savoy Brown and Sophie Thatcher.

In the "spooky teenager" genre, few names are as notable as Carrie White. But rather than give us a by-the-numbers send-up of Stephen King's famous teen heroine, Mike Flanagan's Prime Video miniseries modernizes the cautionary tale of what happens when a youngster is pushed too far by their peers, chillingly bringing the relentless scrutiny and casual cruelty of social media and smartphone culture into the fold.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Summer H. Howell stars as the sheltered titular teen, who has to juggle not only grieving the sudden, untimely loss of her father but also entering the merciless world of public high school and the discovery that she might just be in possession of mysterious telekinetic powers. Given that "The Body" took direct influence from King's original tale and Brian De Palma's 1976 film adaptation, it's no surprise that both that Netflix series and Prime Video's "Carrie" share similar themes of religious extremism, mean-girl viciousness, social isolation, and feminine rage.

If you're looking for more religious horror and cultish creepiness, you don't have to leave Netflix after finishing "The Body"; "Devil in Ohio" is, handily, on the same platform, an eight-episode miniseries adaptation of Daria Polatin’s best-selling book.

Where "The Body" revolves around the cult-like dynamics of a group of Catholic school girls, though, the latter thriller is set within a literal satanic cult, from which the young Mae (Madeleine Arthur) has desperately escaped with a pentagram carved straight into her back. As she awaits foster care placement, Mae finds shelter with hospital psychiatrist Dr. Suzanne Mathis (Emily Deschanel), whose family life and suburban world are turned upside down by the strange occurrences and ominous secrets that chillingly emerge upon the teen girl's arrival.

#3217. ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Turns Chaos & Crime Into Cash & Clout With Record-Shattering Launch

Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics

Taylor Swift and AI investment have proven to be big boosts to the U.S. economy in the recent years. Yet, come Thursday, the mayhem-packed Grand Theft Auto VI is going to be the heavy hitter with record- breaking stats and a possibly legislative long-tail that could truly change the game.

Or, as they’ve been saying repeatedly this midterms-mocking season on Comedy Central’s South America (a.k.a. South Park): “If you ask me, this whole country has gone to sh*t …But hopefully things will get better in November. That’s when Grand Theft Auto VI comes out.”

Exceeding $1.54 billion in pre-order sales, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tracker, the first new game in the GTA video game franchise in 13 years is already the most successful entertainment industry launch ever. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Netflix UK Swoops For Ms Apple's Pre-School Learning Adventures News Jeff Bezos Describes How Amazon Decided On Robert Pattinson As The Next James Bond

Put in franchise perspective, GTA VI’s pre-order haul is just a touch under double the launch of the $800 million snared by 2013’s Grand Theft Auto V, the previous all-time entertainment debut record holder. GTA V, which like GTA VI was pushed back from its originally stated release date, has gone on to sell more than 235 million units. The sometimes grisly GTA V has also proved a massive hit on publisher Rockstar Games‘ lucrative GTA Online multiplayer platform.

To give you an idea of the massive numbers in store here for GTA VI‘s first day when it comes to the big screen, the global box office opening day alone this year on Sony/Marvel Studio’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day was $276.1 million (note that some foreign territories open on Wednesday and Thursday and have their ticket sales rolled into North America’s opening day Friday). Spider-Man: Brand New Day went on to post a global opening weekend of $932 million and that’s the second highest worldwide opening at the B.O. After Avengers: Endgame’s $1.2 billion. Five movies have grossed over $1 billion worldwide year-to-date, Brand New Day being the highest at $2.5 billion, ahead of The Odyssey ($1.8 billion), Toy Story ($1.1 billion), biopic Michael ($1 billion) and Super Mario Galaxy Movie ($1 billion).

At the current trajectory leading to GTA VI going live at midnight local time globally on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, pre-orders are on target to hit sales of 20 million and $2 billion in revenue before the end of the week. Before the end of the year, with day of launch purchases and then holiday shopping factoring in, GTA IV is estimated to bring in around $3 billion, says L.A.-based Wedbush Securities.

“Next to James Bond, there might not be another franchise of this scale that has been as consistent with its brand,” says Larry Vincent, professor of Marketing at USC Marshall School of Business. “It’s like they apprenticed with the Broccoli family,” he adds of the Take-Two Interactive-owned series and the former 007 bosses.

Kinder and gentler in execution than past sex worker killing and explicit content-containing installments of the 1997-launched open sandbox franchise, the still very violent GTA VI finds the detail-rich immersive series returning to the Miami-inspired Vice City. Which means, much like 2002’s single player Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, the ever-expanding crime escapades of lovers Jason and Lucia in this iteration are neon- streaked, car chase-fueled, bullet-loaded and blood-soaked in the sweaty fictional state of Leonida.

Filled to the brim with a satirical and scathing take on American culture. GTA VI is clearly giving the people the blood and circus they want.

Following a leak online, the December 4, 2025 release of the official GTA VI trailer racked up over 93 million views in 24 hours to become the all-time top non-music debut on the Alphabet-owned video platform. Philadelphia-based Comcast this week declared the first 48 hours of GTA VI pre-order downloads that began on November 10 to be “our network’s biggest event and two of its 10 busiest days ever.”

Managing pre-order downloads and expecting a rush of launch-day purchases, stateside internet providers such as Charter‘s Spectrum and Comcast’s Xfinity have been offering customers free speed boosts to prevent digital logjams. Add to that, as Sony put out last minute PS5 software updates, a worry for later in the week is that the internet could slow due to spike in YouTube livestreams and social media posts as players drill into the game.

A true global release, GTA VI nearly crashed Netflix this summer with its well-watched Extended Look featurette. As proof of the streamer’s own clout and reach, GTA VI pre-sales surged once the 27-minute Extended Look dropped on August 27.

Since then, promotion for the game has covered almost every digital, horizontal and vertical surface from L.A. to NYC to London, Paris, Berlin, New Delhi, Hong Kong, Tokyo and Sydney and all points in between.

With skyscrapers, hoardings and murals all over the seven continents displaying GTA VI artwork, product activations soared. Songs from the game have topped playlists too, with a soundtrack score by electronic duo Justice out on December 11.

Going local, the game logo has skinned the outside of the arena of the NBA’s Miami Heat. Inside the Kaseya Center, GTA VI will be all over Wednesday’s “A Night in Vice City” ESPN-broadcast game between the Heat and the Milwaukee Bucks.

No details have been revealed yet as to when the more than $1 billion to develop GTA VI will appear on the GTA Online platform. The presumption is it will likely be deep into 2027 to give Take-Two’s bottom line a multi-quarter leg up.

Take-Two shares gained 6% last week amid the GTA hype, but have since reversed direction. They fell 4% on Tuesday and are now down 20% in 2026 to date as Wall Street has sought to reconcile the runaway success of the GTA franchise with decidedly mixed quarterly financial results. Take-Two aren’t the only ones feeling the pinch. All video game publishers have been scrambling of late to adjust to an evolving consumer marketplace, with mobile and casual games meaningfully eating into the share of traditional console tentpoles.

With that, any deeper bottom line comparisons between MAGA era GTA VI and the Obama Era GTA V become a little bit apples to avocados.

To frustration of some, the 2026 game is only available digitally as opposed to on the more traditional disc of previous GTAs. Which is also why, if you are a gamer or gamer adjacent, you have spent days over the past week downloading the colossal 212GB GTA VI for Thursday’s debut. In anticipation of November 19, which is widely viewed as an adult snow day with millions of fans playing hooky off work to play the game, you may have also been forking out more cash to upgrading your console so you can play GTA VI in either its $79.99 Standard Edition or the $99.99 Ultimate Edition.

It is that money pit mentality from the video game industry that spurned Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY) to put the Power to the Players Act before Congress last month. Still collecting co-sponsors and paused a bit as a newly Democratic-controlled majority prepares to take power, the P2P Act would compel the FCC to ensure that buying a game means it’s the consumer’s, full stop.

“Just based on revenue, the video game industry is larger than global film, global music, and North American sports combined,” the just re-elected South Bronx representing Democrat says. “It’s massive, and historically, it’s been the most affordable form of entertainment,” the Congressman asserts. “My district is hit the hardest by the affordability crisis, and digital-only distribution disproportionately disadvantages the lowest-income consumers, who are more likely to trade and use games to subsidize the purchase of new ones.”

In a stance that runs counter to where Take-Two and much of the industry are taking things, Rep. Torrs adds: “My view is that in a properly functioning marketplace, when you pay for a video game, you should be purchasing the game itself, right? If you pay for it, then you should own it. Simple rule, but increasingly, when you pay for a video game, you are not purchasing the game itself. You are purchasing a license to play the game, and that license can be revoked arbitrarily at the discretion of the gaming company. So, it feels to me like we as consumers are paying higher and higher prices while enjoying fewer and fewer rights, if any rights at all.”

Torres’ bill has a way to go before becoming a law, but it is certainly now part of the cultural conversation sparked by GTA VI‘s mega-release As close to a monoculture moment as we can have in 2026, GTA VI is a conversation even the cops and the Weather Channel have joined:

GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is!🎮Don't confuse virtual entertainment with real-life decisions.Drunk driving, reckless driving, auto theft and violence have real consequences.Keep it in the game. Don't bring it to our streets. pic.twitter.com/Y7PdJFHLsZ

Looks like we have to add Vice City as a location on our app…🌴👀

Another voice in all this belongs to producer and actor Matthew Waterson. Best known as the voice of X-Men ’97‘s Magneto, Waterson is also an alum of the blockbuster Call of Duty franchise and Rockstar’s best selling Red Dead Redemption games.

“They’re such unique properties that people are willing to wait for, people are willing to talk about, think about it and get excited for because they build such rich environments,” Waterson insists of GTA and RDR. “Most other companies at this point don’t have the the time or the money or the capital to do that,”

“These big public companies don’t have the capital expenditure abilities to put 10 years into a huge world concept game if they don’t know it’s going to make money,” says Waterson of risk adverse and cash restricted studios and streamers. “Rockstar have two products that they know are going to make money. Rockstar can do that, and just about nobody else can.”

Anthony D’Alessandro & Dade Hayes contributed to this report

With the holiday season just around the corner, I’m turning to Joanna Gaines for inspiration to get my home ready. The “Fixer Upper” star doesn’t disappoint with her recent Instagram post on styling a mantelpiece with a sweet gingerbread theme.

No mantelpiece? No problem! While I’m lucky enough to have one and will use her creative ideas to curate my own cute display, you can easily adapt the look to create gingerbread-inspired decor anywhere in your home.

In a recent Instagram post, Joanne Gaines sets to work styling a mantelpiece with decorative products available from Magnolia, the lifestyle and home brand she founded with her husband, Chip Gaines.

A post shared by Joanna Gaines (@joannagaines)

When you break it down into stages, creating this look at home is surprisingly simple, whether you splurge on the exact products Gaines uses or opt for budget-friendly alternatives. Here is how to achieve the style both ways.

Gaines starts by building the foundation of the design by intertwining three Real Touch Cedar Mix Garlands, $43 at Magnolia, with red berries (only available in-store). Once she’s happy with the “natural and whimsical” base, she tucks gingerbread houses throughout the greenery.

To make it extra special, she uses Lighted Gingerbread decorations that add a warm glow, mixing two different sizes to add depth and dimension to the display. You can grab the smaller Lighted Cottage Gingerbread House for $25 at Magnolia.

Of course, a festive mantelpiece wouldn’t be complete without a display of stockings for each family member. Here, Gaines uses Marble and Gilded Stocking Holders, $22 at Magnolia, to display her stockings. Rather than sticking to one design, she mixes up the prints for an eclectic look, blending plaid, velvet and winter tulip-printed designs. I love the richness of velvet, so I would personally opt for the luxurious Chanel Velvet Stocking in Winter Moss, $30 at Magnolia.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Even with the stockings up, Gaines hasn’t quite finished her display. The final touch is the Joyeux Noel Candle, $30 at Magnolia, featuring warm notes of cranberry, mandarin and clove — once lit, it will feel like Christmas has well and truly arrived.

I love decorating my home for the holidays, though between buying gifts and hosting, I try to keep a close eye on my budget. While I adore Gaines’ festive decor, I’ve been hunting for ways to get a similar aesthetic for less. Here are six budget-friendly Amazon finds that will bring that same holiday charm to your mantel.

This beautiful Red Berry Garland can be intertwined with a pine garland to create the backdrop for your mantel decor. It measures 8.9 feet and includes two hooks at either end of easy hanging. Besides decorating your mantel, it’s the perfect festive decoration to dress your table, or even your front door.

Drape this Real Touch Norfolk Pine Garland on your mantel with the red berry garland above. Plus, right now, when you buy this pack of two garlands, you can save 31%, so you can layer for a luxurious look.

Why buy one gingerbread house when you can buy a whole village? This set of three houses all includes warm LED lights, creating a cozy village scene when lit. With textured roofs and realistic icing, these pretty gingerbread houses look good enough to eat.

Rather than getting out your tool kit to hammer in a nail, you can hang your Christmas stockings from your mantel with these Christmas Stocking Holders. The set includes a reindeer, snowflake, snowman and Christmas tree hook. And if you don’t have a mantel, place them on a shelf or bookcase.

This elegant coordinated set of six Christmas stockings includes three designs. Two classic green-and-red plaid stockings sit alongside two green and two white velvet designs. All are finished with a feature bow and come complete with a dark green hanging loop.

There’s nothing like a real candle to help you embrace the festive spirit. When lit, this scented soy wax candle will enhance the room with the warming fragrance of cypress, eucalyptus and fig. However, take care where you place the candle when lit, and never leave it unattended when it’s burning.

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. Amazon's early Black Friday sale is bringing some pretty significant discounts on Apple devices, including several of the company's latest releases. The biggest savings are on the M5 MacBook Air, with up to $249 off, though there are plenty of smaller deals worth considering, too, from the AirPods Pro 3 at $179.00 to the Apple Pencil Pro at $99. You'll also find discounts on iPads, the Mac mini, and everyday accessories like the Magic Keyboard, Magic Trackpad, and AirTags. With Apple raising prices across its Mac and iPad lineups in June, citing higher memory chip costs, these sales offer a good opportunity to upgrade without paying full price.

The AirPods Pro 3 are down to $179 from $249, saving you $70 on Apple's latest premium wireless earbuds. They offer improved active noise cancellation over the previous generation, along with redesigned foam-infused ear tips and a heart-rate sensor that tracks workouts without an Apple Watch. They also support Live Translation with a compatible iPhone and carry an IP57 rating for sweat and water resistance. PCMag’s review goes into more detail on how they perform.

The AirPods Max 2, which launched in March, are already down to $449.99 from $549, saving you nearly $100 on Apple's premium over-ear headphones. The biggest upgrade over the original model is the H2 chip, which Apple says makes active noise cancellation up to 1.5 times more effective while introducing features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, and Live Translation. For more on its performance, check out this PCMag review.

The Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS, 42mm) is down to $329 from $399, saving you $70. It covers everything you'd expect from a premium smartwatch, including fitness tracking, health monitoring, notifications, and the ability to take calls when your iPhone is nearby. PCMag gave it an "outstanding" rating in its review and also named it its Gift of the Year for 2026.

If you'd prefer to occasionally leave your iPhone behind, the Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS + Cellular, 42mm) is $70 off, bringing its price down to $429 from $499. It has all the same features as the GPS model but adds cellular connectivity, allowing you to make calls, send messages, and stream music even when your phone isn't nearby (provided you have an active cellular plan).

For a more affordable option, the Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS, 40mm) is down to $199 from $249, saving you $50. It covers the essentials, including workout tracking, daily activity monitoring, and notifications, making it a practical choice if you don't need the Series 12's more advanced health features. Check out PCMag's review for a closer look at what you get for the price.

The Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS + Cellular, 40mm) is also $50 off, bringing its price down to $249 from $299. For an extra $50 over the GPS-only model, you get the convenience of making calls, sending messages, and staying connected without keeping your iPhone nearby, provided you have an active cellular plan. It's worth considering if you regularly go for runs, head to the gym, or step out without your phone but still want to stay reachable.

Apple released the M5 MacBook Air in March with 512GB of base storage, double the previous generation's, along with a faster SSD and an N1 wireless chip that adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Right now, the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air (512GB) is down to $1,249.99 from $1,499. For a closer look at the M5 MacBook Air's performance and features, check out PCMag's review.

If you prefer a more compact laptop but need extra storage, the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with a 1TB SSD is down to $1,399.99 from $1,599, saving you $200. That's twice the storage of the base model, giving you more room for large files, photos, videos, and applications without having to rely as heavily on external drives or cloud storage. You still get the M5 chip, faster SSD performance, and Wi-Fi 7 support, all in a smaller, lighter design.

The M6 Mac mini is down to $949.99 from $1,099, saving you $149 on Apple's latest compact desktop. Its 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU can handle everything from everyday multitasking to photo editing and more demanding creative work, while the upgraded Neural Engine helps with AI-related tasks—Apple says the M6 delivers substantial performance improvements over the earlier M4 model, particularly for graphics and AI workloads. For more on how it performs in everyday use, check out PCMag's review.

The M4 iPad Air launched in March, and the 13-inch model is already down to $949.99 from $1,049, saving you nearly $100. Its M4 chip can comfortably handle demanding tasks like photo editing, digital illustration, and multitasking, while the 13-inch Liquid Retina display gives you plenty of room to work across apps. You also get 256GB of storage for your files and creative projects. For more on what to expect, here's PCMag's review.

If you need more storage for your creative projects, the 13-inch M4 iPad Air with 512GB is $100 off, bringing its price down to $1,149 from $1,249. That's double the storage of the 256GB model, giving you more room for large photo libraries, video projects, downloaded files, and apps without having to rely as heavily on cloud storage.

For those looking for something more powerful, the 11-inch iPad Pro with the M5 chip and 512GB of storage is down to $1,299.99 from $1,399, saving you nearly $100. Along with the faster processor, it offers an Ultra Retina XDR OLED display with ProMotion support for refresh rates up to 120Hz, making it particularly well-suited for creative work, video editing, and other demanding tasks.

The Apple Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad is down to $109 from $129, saving you $20 on a wireless keyboard designed primarily for Mac users. It pairs wirelessly over Bluetooth and can be recharged using USB-C. For a closer look at all that it has to offer, check out PCMag's review.

The Magic Trackpad is down to $130 from $149, taking $19 off an accessory that brings the Multi-Touch gestures and Force Touch pressure sensing of a MacBook trackpad to a desktop setup, across an edge-to-edge glass surface. It connects wirelessly over Bluetooth and has a rechargeable battery that lasts about a month between charges. You can read PCMag's full review to see how it stacks up.

The Apple Pencil Pro is down to $99 from $129, saving you $30 on Apple's most feature-rich stylus. It adds squeeze and barrel-roll gestures, haptic feedback, and Find My support to Apple's stylus lineup, and it pairs and charges magnetically along the side of a compatible iPad, including the M4 iPad Air featured above. For more on its strengths and limitations, check out PCMag's review.

The second-generation AirTag, released in January, keeps the original's size so existing holders still fit, while a new Ultra Wideband chip extends Precision Finding range by up to 50% and a redesigned speaker plays 50% louder. Right now, its four-pack is down to $79.99 from $99.99, which works out to $20 per tag, compared with $29 for a single AirTag. PCMag's review offers a more detailed look at how it holds up in everyday use.

The Apple Magic Mouse is down to $59.99 from $79.99, saving you $20 on Apple's wireless mouse with a Multi-Touch surface that lets you swipe between pages and scroll through documents using simple finger gestures. It connects to your Mac over Bluetooth and has a rechargeable battery.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Among the deals listed here, the M5 MacBook Air with 512 of storage has one of the larger discounts at $249 off, bringing its price down to $1,249.99, from $1499.

For most people, the Apple Watch SE 3 at $199 is a good starting point, covering everyday fitness tracking, notifications, and essential health features without the higher price of the Series 12. If you want more advanced health monitoring and a more premium smartwatch experience, the Series 12 at $329 is worth considering.

It’s the top time of the year to upgrade your wearable

I've been covering wearables deals for years, and November is hands-down the top time of the year to upgrade your smartwatch or fitness tracker. With that in mind, I've rounded up my top eleven early Black Friday smartwatch deals so far, with picks from Garmin, Apple, Fitbit, and Samsung.

The biggest savings are on the Garmin Instinct 3 AMOLED, with a massive 44% off. This drops the price from $449 to only $249. Not only is the Instinct 3 one of Garmin's toughest-built models, but it's also one of my all-time favorite smartwatches for logging outdoor adventures.

Find more details on this deal and all the rest below.

This is the lowest price I've seen for the Garmin Instinct 3 sold for since reviewing it nearly two years ago. The watch comes in several variations, including the AMOLED-sporting one shown here and a solar-powered model with a lower-quality display, which is also on sale; see below. I prefer this one because battery life is nearly as good as the Solar model, but the display is much easier to read in bright daylight or through goggles/sunglasses.

The Instinct 3 Solar is also marked down, but the deal isn't as good as the AMOLED model. Nevertheless, $100 off one of the longest-lasting smartwatches on the market today is nothing to sneeze at. Seriously, with enough time in the sun, this bad boy stays powered for up to a month on a single charge.

The Vivoactive 6 is one of Garmin's most comfortable, stylish, and well-rounded smartwatches, and $50 off is a decent discount for a model that doesn't go on sale all that often. A reliable fitness and sleep tracker with up to a week of battery life, the Vivoactive 6 also offers handy smart features like onboard music storage and NFC tap-to-pay.

The Garmin Forerunner 570 represents the upper-middle tier of the brand's running-centric line-up. Personally, I think it's the best of the bunch for most people thanks to rock-solid GPS and heart rate tracking, support for the brand's best training and recovery tools, solid battery performance, a bright touchscreen, and a sporty, comfortable design. Like the Vivoactive 6, this one also doesn't go on sale often.

The Garmin Venu 4 is probably the brand's nearest competitor to the Apple Watch 12, which also happens to be on sale right now (see below). It combines Garmin's most advanced training chops and tools with a small but useful smattering of smart features, all neatly packed in a durable, premium metal case.

If the Venu 4 is Garmin's answer to the Apple Watch 12, then the Garmin Venu X1 is the brand's retort to the Ultra series. One of the only square-shaped Garmins on the market, the X1 boasts a massive, bright AMOLED screen and an impressively thin case design. As you might expect from a smartwatch with a retail price of $699, you're getting all of Garmin's best fitness features in this one, along with niceties like NFC and music storage. Oh, and like the Instinct 3, this is the lowest price I've seen the Venu X1 go for yet.

Garmin isn't the only brand with tempting smartwatch deals. The brand-new Apple Watch Series 12 is already discounted by a healthy amount, despite launching just two months ago. In fact, this is the lowest it's been sold for yet. That said, based on prior holiday sales, I'm willing to bet this will go as low as $299 as we get a little closer to December.

The Apple Watch SE 3 may be entry-level, but it's still a plenty-good smartwatch, and frankly, my favorite model in the lineup. Deal-wise, similar to the Series 12 above, I'd be willing to bet the SE 3 will see an even bigger discount the closer we get to the holidays. After all, it dropped to just $149 last year, a ludicrously good price.

The Fitbit Charge 6 has been around for a while and was even recently replaced by the more capable Fitbit Edge. However, the Charge 6 remained my top pick as the best fitness tracker for most people for three years straight (up until I reviewed the Edge). The reason is simple. The Charge 6 is lightweight, comfortable, fairly reliable, and long-lasting. It supports NFC and mirrored smartphone notifications. Is the screen tiny? Yes. Does it lack an altimeter for elevation data? Also yes. But for a lot of folks, those drawbacks likely won't matter much. That said, the Charge 6 will probably drop in price further in the coming weeks. I predict a lowest sale price of $99.

The Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 is one model removed from the latest release, but let me be straight with you: I reviewed both, and the difference between the Galaxy Watch 8 and Galaxy Watch 9 is minimal at best. Moreover, it remains one of the best smartwatches on the market today, up there with the Apple Watch and Google Pixel Watch 5 (which sadly isn't on sale right now).

#3212. 10 Shows Like 'MobLand' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Crime dramas often attract big stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

While families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other shows mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

Theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

Another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's company town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the new sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated plan to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

MobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

Tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he says he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates new maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Company all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

Best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other shows on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

The great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

Adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a new adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

#3210. Former Apple chairman Arthur Levinson files to sell $31.8 million in company stock

Arthur Levinson, who currently serves as Apple’s lead independent director, informed the SEC today of his plans to sell 90,000 shares of Apple stock worth approximately $31.8 million. Here are the details.

If you’ve been following Apple for a while, you likely know the name Arthur Levinson, as he served as the company’s chairman from 2011 until September of this year, when Tim Cook took over as executive chairman as part of the leadership transition that saw John Ternus become CEO.

Back in May, Levinson made headlines when he sold 250,000 Apple shares for approximately $71.2 million. Three weeks later, he sold another 50,000 shares for $15.55 million. On the same day, he also transferred another 65,000 shares as a gift. Still, he retained approximately 3.7 million directly held shares in the company.

Today, Levinson informed the SEC in a Form 144 filing of his plans to sell 90,000 common shares with an aggregate market value of $31,765,885.00, though the disclosure did not specify how many Apple shares he currently holds. The shares are held in The Homeplace Trust, with Levinson acting as trustee and handling the proposed sale on the trust’s behalf.

The filing lists all shares as acquired in cash on February 27, 2001, though it does not disclose how much Levinson originally paid for them. For reference, Apple stock was trading at approximately $0.29 per share on a split-adjusted basis on that date, compared to roughly $353 today.

Importantly, Apple has undergone three stock splits since then, meaning the 90,000 shares listed in the filing don’t necessarily correspond to the number of shares Levinson originally purchased in 2001.

According to the filing, the transaction was expected to take place today through Charles Schwab. However, it is worth noting that Form 144 is only a notice of a proposed sale, meaning the filing does not confirm that the transaction has already been completed.
