#3086. The Simple Trick That Keeps Poached Eggs Perfectly Intact

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Avoid eggs that fall apart in the pot when you use this genius egg-poaching hack.

Poaching eggs takes practice, but even the gentlest drop into a simmering (never rolling) pot of water can yield sloppy results. It turns out the reason your poached eggs look less like the neat, tidy protein puff you see on food magazine covers and more like a Jackson Pollock has to do with the egg’s structure, not your kitchen skills.

One simple, no-fuss step is all that stands between you and perfect poached eggs, according to a bona fide egg expert I spoke with—and then validated with my not-so-scientific at-home test.

Lisa Steele is a fifth-generation chicken keeper and author of Fresh Eggs Daily and In Season: 125+ Sweet and Savory Recipes Celebrating Simple, Fresh Ingredients. She talked me through the single, foolproof step that makes stovetop egg poaching dead simple.

Picture it: a pot full of water, maybe with a dash of distilled vinegar, at the gentlest simmer so you don’t subject your delicate egg to a tornado of activity when you submerge it. You painstakingly crack the egg into a shallow bowl first and carefully slip it into the pot. Regardless of your good intentions, the egg then clouds the water and turns all wispy, like some sort of blond dementor.

You haven’t done anything wrong here; you’ve just failed to understand an egg’s basic structure. “There are actually two components of the egg white, or albumen,” Steele explains. “There’s the thicker part of the white which encases the yolk, and then there’s a separate, thinner layer of egg white around that. It’s the thinner part of the egg white that will spread and turn wispy when you drop an egg into the water.”

The thing is, you can easily get rid of the thin, watery white part of your egg using one simple tool you’ve probably got in a drawer somewhere and about a minute of your time. Set a small mesh strainer over a cup or bowl, crack the egg into it, and wait.

“Straining an egg removes the thinner whites that likely won’t adhere to the rest of the egg and result in shaggy, wispy threads,” Steele says. “It won’t affect the flavor outcome of your poached egg, but it is purely for appearance’s sake.” (And potentially your sanity’s or sense of accomplishment’s sake, I might add.)

While the egg’s flavor stays unchanged, for Benedict lovers, straining the egg first slightly improves the white-to-yolk ratio in the poached result and makes the texture more consistent, while also creating a tidy, photogenic package.

Once your raw egg is in the strainer, you may notice nothing happens right away, and you may feel the urge to move the egg around a bit to get things going. But don’t zhush, which threatens to scramble the egg. Simply wait for gravity to do its thing; it takes about a minute. It’s akin to what happens when separating whites from yolks, except here you’re separating whites from whites.

“Let the thin part of the egg white drip down into the bowl,” Steele says, “then gently slide the egg into the simmering water.” The strainer can also serve as a handy vessel for transferring the egg, especially if you’re making only one. If you’re doing multiple eggs and don’t want to risk cooking any remaining white onto the mesh by submerging it, place the strained egg in a small, shallow bowl as usual before easing it into the water. Without the thin, watery white part, you’ll notice a discernible textural difference in the egg even when raw.

The straining step alone can almost completely change your poached egg game in an instant, but for the best results, follow the best poaching protocol. You don’t want a full pot of water at a rolling boil like you would for pasta. “Fill a pot or saucepan with a few inches of water and bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to low so the water is just barely simmering with small bubbles floating to the surface,” Steele advises.

Creating a little whirlpool will further help your remaining egg white stay snug. “Using a wooden spoon or silicone spatula, swirl the water, then gently slide the egg into the center of the whirlpool as you keep swirling for another few seconds around the egg until the egg white turns milky and starts to set up around the yolk,” Steele says. “At this point, you can push the egg to one side, add another egg into the center and repeat the process.”

A soft-poached egg takes about three minutes, and because you’ve removed the watery part of the egg white, you’ll get a nice firm structure to hold the still-runny yolk — the poached egg ideal.

Since poaching is a delicate process, no matter your new straining habit and how strictly you follow the recommended procedure, “using the freshest eggs possible is very important when you are poaching because the egg white gets even more thin and watery as the egg ages,” Steele says. “The membrane holding the yolk together also weakens, making the yolk more susceptible to breaking.” So if you don’t have them on hand already, get yourself a strainer and some fresh eggs and put this newfound tidbit to the personal test.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is also down to its lowest ever price, dropping from $1,899 to $1,549 at Amazon. Or, if you'd rather something traditional, the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is now $1,049 at Amazon. The iPhone 18 Pro Max can be had for just $100 at T-Mobile and AT&T, so long as you match the sign-up criteria.

But it's not just Samsung and Apple devices that have had their prices reduced. Check below for the best Black Friday phone deals currently available, from retailers and carriers alike.

T-Mobile is giving away the iPhone Duo, and you don't even need to trade in an old device. You will need to sign up for a qualifying T-Mix plan, though, and use seven Picks perks every month.

Alternatively, you can save $1,200 by signing up to a T-Mix plan with three perks. Just trade in an eligible device in any condition to qualify.

You can save $1,200 on the iPhone Duo at AT&T, so long as you sign up for a Premium 2.0 Plan (or higher) and trade in an eligible device.

That same trade-in deal is available for other iPhones at AT&T, which means you can get the iPhone 18 Pro for free or the iPhone 18 Pro Max for $100 (spread over 36 months). Again, trade in an eligible device and sign up for a Premium 2.0 Plan.

T-Mobile is also giving away iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, again without needing to trade in your old device. Simply sign up to a T-Mix plan with five Picks, and the phone is yours.

Or if you'd rather reduce your monthly bill, you can save $1,200 when you sign up for a new line on three-pick T-Mix plan. However, you will need to port your number from another carrier, or trade in an eligible device (in any condition).

There's no iPhone Air 2 yet, but if you want a phone that's slim, lightweight and durable to the extreme this is the one to pick. It may only have one camera, but it still has all the things that make iPhones great.

Since the iPhone 18 isn't due until next year, the iPhone 17 is your best non-Pro option right now. The good news is that Walmart has knocked the price down by $70. Just keep in mind that this deal is locked to Walmart's Straight Talk.

If you need something a little cheaper, there's the iPhone 16. It may be older, but it's still got a lot to offer in the camera and performance departments. Just be warned, this handset is also locked to the Straight Talk MVNO.

The iPhone 17e makes some sacrifices, like the fact it only has one main camera, but it's still a solid choice if you're looking for a low-cost iPhone. It features MagSafe, Apple Intelligence, 256GB of storage as standard and offers powerful A19 performance.

The first Apple e-Series model may be older, but it still has a lot going for it too. In fact, the only key differences between it and the iPhone 17e are the lack of MagSafe and the fact it has an A18 chip.

Samsung's take on the passport-shaped foldable is easily one of the best phones of the year. The shorter, wider design is comfortable to use, and the anti-glare screen makes it perfect for watching movies or working no matter the conditions. The battery could be better, and the lack of telephoto lens isn't ideal, but this is a fantastic deal on a foldable you can buy right now.

If you'd prefer a bigger screen and telephoto zoom camera, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is the option for you. It's a little bit more expensive, but you get more screen space, camera resolution and battery capacity for your money.

The Z Flip 8 is less exciting by comparison, but it still gets you the foldable experience in a compact form. You have the normal-size 6.9-inch phone display, a pair of solid cameras and a cover display that can run full Android apps without requiring you to flip the thing open.

If you want a book-style foldable with a heavy discount, there's always the Galaxy Z Fold 7. It's the same shape and size as the Z fold 8 Ultra, though it lacks the Flex Titanium crease-free display, higher performance and larger batteries of the newer model. But it's also a few hundred dollars cheaper.

If the latest Galaxy S26 is up your alley, Walmart has knocked it back down to $799, reversing the recent price hike. You get the latest Galaxy AI features, a 6.3-inch OLED display, a 4,300 mAh battery, 50MP main camera, 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage standard.

If you want a bigger screen and less-flashy hardware, the S25 Plus has your back — and a price to match. It has a 6.7-inch display, 45W charging, 50MP rear cameras, a 4,900 mAh battery, and all the latest Galaxy AI features.

The super thin Galaxy S25 Edge is still available, and it's been given a nice Black Friday discount. So if you want a skinny phone with two solid cameras running Android, now's your chance.

If Samsung's price hikes have you down, the Galaxy S26 FE is the perfect solution — offering flagship level specs at a newly-discounted price. For your money you get solid camera and battery performance, including a telephoto lens, and a large 6.7-inch display and the latest Galaxy AI software.

The Fan Edition lineup is a great way to get flagship features at a discount, and the S25 FE was no exception. It may not be as new or powerful as the S26 FE, but the physical differences between the two are fairly minimal. That said, I do prefer this model's more premium-looking back glass.

The Pixel 11 is more than half off over at Mint Mobile, and the only catch is you need to sign up for Mint's Unlimited data plan — at a cost of $180 for a year. Though that still makes this an excellent discount, especially if you like AI features and speedy access to Android updates.

If you want more out of your Pixel, Mint has knocked $505 off the cost of the Pixel 11 Pro. For your money you get the HiLight notification alert, better cameras, a brighter display and strong battery life. But again you do need that $180 unlimited plan.

If you want a larger screen, the Pixel 11 Pro XL is the exact same phone, only bigger and with a larger battery. It's discounted from $1,299 to $794 at Mint.

It may not be the most exciting foldable around, nor is this the biggest discount, but if you want a Pixel Fold device this is the best discount around right now. Just be aware that you need to pay an extra $180 for Mint's Unlimited plan to be eligible.

One of the best cheap phones you can buy, the Nothing 4a Pro offers great cameras and battery life, including a 50MP telephoto lens — which is a rarity at this price point. Also included is the custom Glyph Matrix LED display on the back, Nothing's latest AI features and solid performance.

If you want the latest and most compact foldable, the Razr 2026 is on sale at Mint Mobile. However, the discount requires you to sign up for a 12-month Unlimited plan for $180. Still, you get a large foldable display, strong performance, a crazy 4,800 mAh battery and a range of Motorola's AI features.

If you want a cheap compact foldable without the added data plan, the 2025 Motorola Razr is the one to pick. You get a large bright foldable display, an assortment of AI features and a cover display that can run all your Android apps — even ones that may not be optimized for it.

If the standard Razr isn't cutting it for you, the Plus model has a little more to offer. It's got a faster 165Hz refresh rate, a 4,000 mAh battery, 12GB of RAM, 256GB of storage, and a pair of 50MP (main and telephoto) cameras. Plus a 32MP selfie camera.

The Razr Ultra is almost half price right now, with the same 165Hz refresh rate, 512GB of storage, a boosted 16GB of RAM, a 50MP selfie camera and a crazy 4,500 nits of screen brightness.

#3083. Oura’s new feature could help you kick jet lag – how to enable it

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Oura just launched a Jet Lag Plan to help you stay alert when you switch time zones, whether you're traveling for business or pleasure.

Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.

Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura announced Jet Lag Plan, a new feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.

Also: Oura Ring users may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know

Jet Lag Plan takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering new time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

Ring users will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Plan accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

“Two people on the same flight can get different plans, because guidance reflects your itinerary, your typical sleep schedule, and your chronotype,” Oura writes in a blog post. The chronotype refers to Oura’s sleep chronotype, which categorizes users into six types (early morning, morning, early evening, and so on) based on their historical sleep activity.

After adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The plan is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. Users can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Plan is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

Go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Plan to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

Get help instantly, even if you're too far away from your phone

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

This year, I’ve tested an assortment of Bluetooth trackers ranging from popular options like the AirTag 2 and Pixel Tag all the way to more niche ones like the Statik SmartCard Incognito and Nomad Leather Mag Wallet. Yet, the ones that really stood out the most were the Pebblebee Clip 5 and Halo.

These two trackers are getting even better thanks to Pebblebee’s new service, Alert Dispatch, which loops a real human into the safety experience during emergencies. The Clip 5 and Halo can already send priority notifications and messages to your emergency contacts, but Alert Dispatch goes the extra mile by having a trained dispatch agent reach out by text to check whether the individual who triggered the alert is all right.

Frankly, it makes them function a lot like a lifeline when a person has fallen and is unable to reach out for help — especially for an elderly family member, someone who lives on their own, or someone with a disability. This lifesaving feature adds more peace of mind, and it puts both the AirTag 2 and Pixel Tag on notice. Here’s why.

The Pebblebee Clip 5 is a rugged AirTag alternative that lets you keep track of its location, with a rechargeable battery that can last up to 12 months. It also functions almost like a lifeline device that sends its location to people in your alert profile so they can get additional help.Price check: $34.99 @ Pebblebee

Pebblebee’s Bluetooth trackers already have a huge advantage by alerting emergency contacts when they’re triggered, but the live location sharing and Safety Circle updates currently available are now being supplemented with a real human agent from Pebblebee's dispatch partner, Noonlight.

When an alert is triggered, a trained agent reaches out via text first to confirm the person is safe. If there’s no reply, the agent follows up with an emergency phone call — and after three consecutive unanswered calls, the dispatcher attempts to send emergency responders directly to their last known location. They’ll also pass along a pre-filled Emergency Profile and responder notes.

Meanwhile, up to eight trusted contacts in a user's Safety Circle can monitor their live location and dispatch status in real time through the Safety Portal. Those with the Clip 5 and Halo also get a Private Check-In feature that lets them connect directly with a dispatch agent without alerting their Safety Circle.

While it shares the same common functions as any Bluetooth tracker, the Pebblebee Halo packages in a bright flashlight, 130dB siren, and a dedicated SOS button to send out help to the contacts in your Safety Circle.Price check: $32.99 @ Pebblebee

Like I mentioned before, the Clip 5 and Halo come with a free Alert service from Pebblebee that sends a notification to one person in your Safety Circle when they’re triggered. For additional users, there’s an Alert Live subscription that normally costs $24.99 for an entire year (or $2.99/month) and increases it to five trusted contacts in your Safety Circle (along with live location sharing).With Alert Dispatch, though, Pebblebee offers three subscription tiers based on how many people (seats) you want to cover. They consist of the following:

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The $49.99/year subscription for Alert Dispatch is more than the $24.99/year cost for Alert Live, but that difference means that a human dispatcher can still send out help if none of the contacts in the Safety Circle are available. That alone makes it perfect for older adults, especially those living on their own or simply too far away from other family members.

While the AirTag 2 and Pixel Tag are some of the most findable trackers on the market, thanks in part to the pinpoint accuracy of ultra-wideband, they lack the emergency response action that Pebblebee’s trackers offer with Alert Dispatch. Timing makes all the difference, and when someone is in dire need and can’t get to a phone for help, this fallback could be the thing that makes the most difference.

#3079. Own 2 Android phones? Google may let you switch service fast – like iPhone Handoff

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

If Android Fast Switch works like iPhone Handoff, one eSIM can be quickly switched between two phones.

In iOS 27, Apple announced iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows users to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones. Text strings in Google’s SIM Manager app suggest the company is preparing a similar feature for compatible Android phones, according to Android Authority.

Code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch. Little information is currently available about the feature’s limitations, including which phones or mobile carriers may not be compatible.

Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart

On Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not currently support iPhone Handoff.

However, the code strings uncovered by Android Authority show that Android’s Fast Switch will work similarly to iPhone Handoff, in that users must be signed in to both devices under the same Google account for the feature to work.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two users, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

If Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

Features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

Also: Google Wallet turns your Android phone into a digital house key

In that case, one person can keep up with two phones without paying for two phone service lines through their carrier. Still, users will incur a fee, as T-Mobile charges $5/month for iPhone Handoff, while Verizon charges $10/month.

#3078. Prediction: Colette Kress Is More Vital to Nvidia’s Future Than Her Interim CEO Title Implies

A fundamental shift in Nvidia's corporate strategy could slow down the artificial intelligence boom.

By Daniel Foelber – Updated Nov 18, 2026 at 6:45AM EST

It has been a brutal month for Nvidia (NVDA -0.36%) investors. Concerns about sustained cash burn among hyperscalers such as Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet sparked a widespread sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, especially semiconductor stocks. Then matters got much, much worse.

On Nov. 8, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair that U.S. officials are looking into for potential national security concerns. After market close on Nov. 11, The New York Times reported that Huang had a different affair with an Nvidia employee. News of yet another affair with a separate employee surfaced on Nov. 12. That same day, Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO -- effective immediately -- with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO.

Nvidia's CEO transition has market-rippling effects, given Huang has been CEO since the company's founding 33 years ago and the sheer size of Nvidia and its impact on the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.02%), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +0.60%), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -0.54%). Few CEOs carry as much importance. The only comparable examples are fellow founders at large tech-focused companies like Elon Musk at Tesla and Space Exploration Technologies, Mark Zuckerberg at Meta Platforms, or long-tenured prominent CEOs like Hock Tan at Broadcom. But Huang takes the cake given the length of his tenure and Nvidia's valuation.

Huang's shoes are arguably too big to fill by one person alone. Here's why Kress' leadership now matters more than ever, even if she eventually passes the baton to a long-term CEO, and what that could mean for the stock going forward.

One of the most effective leadership dynamics is a visionary, borderline unbridled CEO with a bounty of big ideas contrasted with a shrewd realist that possesses unique technical, financial, operating, or accounting skills. Examples include Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, with Jobs pushing big ideas and Tim Cook acting as Apple's master operator.

Or Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg, with Sandberg serving as chief operating officer of Meta Platforms from 2008 to 2022. Without Sandberg, there's a good argument that Meta Platforms wouldn't be the streamlined cash cow it is today.

My personal favorite example is Walt Disney’s eponymous founder and president and his brother, Roy O. Disney. Because Roy was so good at managing the company's credit lines and financial obligations, Walt was free to take chances on risky endeavors, enough of which paid off to create an entertainment giant.

In all three examples, the visionary captured Wall Street's spotlight, but the savvy operator provided the glue that held the business together.

In many ways, Kress counterbalanced Huang's visionary bets with pragmatic financial discipline. I suspect she was a major catalyst behind Nvidia's massive dividend increases and stock buybacks. After all, it was her comments during Nvidia's GTC 2026 conference that fueled my prediction that Nvidia would make a substantial dividend increase in 2026 and then a second correct prediction that Nvidia would surpass Apple in stock buybacks and dividends.

Reports indicate that Kress may have helped Nvidia commit $105 billion in credit to OpenAI rather than $250 billion and that she questioned the looseness of Nvidia's lending practices toward start-ups and AI cloud providers like neoclouds. It remains to be seen how true these reports are. But if you've tuned into Nvidia's earnings calls and presentations over the years, it's fairly clear that Kress comes across as more of a straightforward, often dry but highly capable executive compared to Huang's promotional, arrogant, but undeniably brilliant persona. My guess is that Kress has done a fair share of checking and balancing Huang behind the scenes, far more than she has been given credit for.

Huang has been instrumental in accelerating the AI build-out beyond hyperscalers to neoclouds and AI start-ups through direct lending practices, as well as plans to partner with a consortium of financial institutions to offer $500 billion in AI infrastructure financing. The only problem is that many AI start-ups haven't yet shown they can consistently turn a profit -- especially high-profile neoclouds like Nebius Group and CoreWeave.

Under Kress, I predict Nvidia's role in the AI build-out becomes much more hands-off. Up to this point, Nvidia has basically been running around Silicon Valley, handing out jars of lighter fluid for start-ups to throw onto the raging AI infrastructure bonfire. Kress could favor a more financially disciplined approach that prioritizes high cash flows over risky bets. That could slow Nvidia's growth rate, but it could also lead to gradual compounding over time rather than a cyclical boom followed by a downturn. Nvidia will likely miss out on some big moonshot bets it would have cashed in on under Huang, but it could also avoid some costly mistakes. And in the end, this dynamic may appeal more to investors who are confident in AI adoption over the long term but feel that the pace of progress has been too hot and too fast.

If Nvidia's growth slows but it retains its ultra-high margins, then it wouldn't be surprising if Nvidia continued to aggressively buy back stock and raised its dividend under Kress. Under that framework, Nvidia could transform from a high-octane growth stock into a balanced company tailor-made for value investors -- as Nvidia trades at just 19.7 times earnings and 16.7 times forward earnings estimates.

Risk-taking beats caution when the bets pay off, which they mostly have for Nvidia. So it's understandable why the stock is down as much as it is. But a less risky strategy could also make Nvidia far less vulnerable to an AI spending downturn.

I wouldn't be surprised if Kress plays an integral role in prolonging the AI boom by taking a slower and steadier approach rather than Huang's full-throttle innovative spirit. This approach could make Nvidia a lot more boring, but it could also pay off for long-term investors willing to endure this period of volatility.

That said, Huang's sudden resignation has fundamentally challenged Nvidia's investment thesis. There's a ton of uncertainty as to how the company will perform under new management, whether it is caught flat-footed and loses market share and talent to competitors, and whether national security breaches will hinder Nvidia's ability to sell chips in China. For those reasons, I think it's totally fair for investors to hold Nvidia and keep it on a watch list until there's more clarity on where Nvidia could be headed from here.

Despite hacking causing some problems for websites, the dire predictions for widespread Nov. 17 catastrophe appeared not to have come true. An emergency alert did air on radio and TV.

As global conspiracy theories go, this was a juicy one.

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, at around 2:20 p.m. ET, the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Communications Commission conducted a test of the Emergency Alert System. That’s when all hell was supposed to break loose. At least, that’s what you might have believed if you only relied on social media.

The good news: The world didn’t break at that time despite fears. The bad news: Some troubling activity did, in fact, happen, even if it may have been unrelated or the result of opportunistic hackers taking advantage of the anxiety. Attackers targeted hundreds of websites with malware seeking to hijack data from credit card transactions, Apple software or cryptocurrency transactions. Sites affected included CNN, IKEA, Fox News and Zoom.

Apple and Google also experienced issues on Tuesday, but it’s unclear if those are related to the hacking that affected websites. Apple’s System Status page reported outages of App Store, Apple Music and iCloud services among others, while some Google users reported issues with their email.

Coming just days after an abrupt and disruptive government-ordered shutdown of air travel in the US and technical issues that caused an unwelcome outage of widely used Microsoft workplace software, the hacking and the government’s alert test happened in an atmosphere of heightened anxiety.

Videos across Facebook, Instagram and TikTok floated the theory that this emergency test signals a catastrophe was coming, potentially stemming from a cyberattack or a digital disruption that could knock out electricity, internet and other services. Many scrambled to buy emergency supplies, pointing to the need for a 90-day stockpile of food, water, cash and essential medicines in case hackers wipe out bank accounts and shut down the web.

Similar rumors spread globally, as the governments of France, the UK and Canada have put renewed attention on the importance of households being able to survive a potential weather-related crisis or technological disaster.

How extreme did the conspiracy theories get? Some cited a 2023 Simpsons episode as proof, which referenced a massive Nov. 17 blackout in Lisa’s future, even though it didn’t mention a year.

For Gen Xers and Boomers, this panic could feel familiar. Leading up to the year 2000, there were fears that a potential computer-related disaster, known as Y2K, would cause widespread chaos and disruption, based on the belief that older digital systems couldn’t handle the calendar change. The new year ended with only minor glitches, thanks to a significant global effort to update computer systems to avoid the bug.

Before we delve into the suspicions, let’s start with a bit of debunking: CNET spoke with multiple experts in disaster preparedness and cyberattacks, who all cautioned against letting our guard down, no matter what the date. But remember that no federal agency or institution has mentioned a blackout.

Richard Mariano, a protective intelligence expert at Kronus Intelligence, who spent nearly three decades with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, said that people share all sorts of things that get picked up and go viral. “Then it creates panic where panic is not necessary,” he said.

Mariano said too many people are spreading fear rather than seeking the truth. “On every one of these social media posts that is suspect or has some form of conspiratorial edge to them: source it, source it, source it.”

The Emergency Alert System message scheduled for Nov. 17 was similar to the public tests Americans have experienced since 1963, (PDF) when the Emergency Broadcast System replaced an older radio-based warning system called CONELRAD. In 1997, the Emergency Broadcast System was replaced by the EAS, part of FEMA’s Integrated Public Alert and Warning System, which broadcasts emergency alerts to any wireless device in the country, including phones, radios and televisions. The system was designed for the president to communicate with US households within 10 minutes of a national emergency.

The Nov. 17 test consisted of a nationwide EAS message issued by FEMA, noting that no public action is required. The test included standard alert tones to support accessibility for those who are deaf or hard of hearing and lasted about a minute. This time around, wireless emergency alerts were not triggered on mobile phones. After the alert, programming resumed as normal on TV, radio and other broadcast channels.

Many equate the emergency system with threats of nuclear war, but it could also be used to alert people to a major weather event, a national cyberattack or even AMBER alerts at the local level (without a presidential message). So it’s natural there might be some anxiety.

“With this event simulating an activation of an emergency notification system, it would be a logical next step to worry about what happens if something bad happens during that test,” said Robby Winchester, chief global professional services officer at SpecterOps, a Virginia-based security company,

But, all in all, these system tests are routine. Local stations conduct a weekly test, and federal law requires a nationwide EAS test every three years. In addition to helping people get used to responding to alerts, the tests also allow the government to identify potential technical or operational issues it needs to fix before an actual emergency alert.

Representatives from the FCC and FEMA did not respond to a request for comment.

Another factor that helped spark conspiracy theories was a Pentagon order requiring military bases to stock enough supplies for 90 days without outside support. Dubbed “Fortress America,” the initiative memo (PDF) was released in late September but got more attention as the November date approached.

The timing of that memo coincided with the UK launching a campaign on Oct. 22 called Be Ready, urging citizens to keep enough supplies (PDF) such as water, food, medical kits and pet products to last at least three days. Other countries, including Japan, Sweden and about a dozen more, are also urging citizens to prepare for emergencies.

Still, the blackout rumor isn’t solely driven by government communications. Heightened global instability over the past few months has also played a major role. Just in the last month, the Federal Aviation Administration called a nationwide ground stop on all departing flights; a major Microsoft Outlook outage kept millions of people from working; PHP vulnerabilities exposed websites to hacking; and cyberattacks have targeted supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe.

On the financial side, Nvidia’s CEO scandal led to a stock plunge and fears of an AI bust, while Paraguay just experienced a major digital bank collapse that froze millions of accounts. The ongoing wars in Iran and Ukraine have sparked national security concerns, and floods in Nepal and fires in Indonesia demonstrate the increased dangers of climate change.

Though there’s never been a nationwide power outage in the US (several regional outages have been triggered by overloaded lines and software bugs), The New York Times reports that there’s still no comprehensive plan for what to do if the country goes completely dark.

All the online chatter surrounding Nov. 17 raised concerns that warnings of a potential cyberattack might inadvertently trigger one.

Winchester said that even though there’s no specific information indicating an imminent crisis, “it is common for attackers to use current events of all types to help with achieving successful attacks.” The upside? If people are being spurred by government notices and their anxiety over global instability to prepare emergency supplies, it could actually help in the event of a real threat or disaster.

Regardless of whether you bought into the Nov. 17 conspiracy theories, it doesn’t hurt to have some supplies on hand, which could be useful in the event of a digital disruption or weather event, even if it doesn’t involve nuclear weapons or hackers.

“We live in a world where there are many threats to our communities, our families and ourselves,” said Philip Farina, chief advisor for Risky Business and a federal law enforcement veteran. “Understanding the basics of self-reliance is important. Even preparing for a residential fire, which is very common, can help to save lives and protect us better.”

You don’t need to buy enough for 90 days off the grid (and most of us can’t afford that), but it’s recommended that families have at least three days’ worth of food and supplies. Some of the basics listed on Ready.gov’s Build a Kit page include:

While warnings from governments can spark panic and distrust, they can be beneficial at a time when we’re so reliant on the internet and cell service, which can be easily disrupted. Mariano said it’s worth being prepared in the “old-fashioned ways.”

#3074. Did Avalanche’s New NYSE Deal Just Make Solana and XRP Irrelevant?

This lesser-known blockchain just scored a huge collaboration with the New York Stock Exchange.

By Alex Carchidi – Nov 18, 2026 at 6:50AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Avalanche ›

The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and its owner, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE -1.11%), just handed the cryptocurrency Avalanche (AVAX -1.98%) a central role in their plan to launch a new exchange for tokenized stocks. On Nov. 9, Ava Labs, Avalanche's developer, announced it would provide blockchain technology for a new NYSE-affiliated venue for those tokens. This is the best news that the coin's holders have gotten in recent memory, but its price was little changed for the seven days ended Nov. 13.

The NYSE deal immediately looks like bad news for two other cryptocurrencies that have been positioning themselves as the preferred solution for this exact niche. Apparently, the NYSE was influenced by properties like Avalanche's speed, throughput, and regulatory tooling. Yet Solana (SOL +0.86%) is dramatically ahead of Avalanche on the first two, and XRP's (XRP +1.35%) network, the XRP Ledger (XRPL), has built strong compliance tools directly into its systems. So did Avalanche and the NYSE deal just make both of those coins irrelevant?

Talking about the choice of Avalanche, NYSE executive Dennis Lee said that the company wanted to pick a blockchain solution that offered predictable costs and strong control over the permissible participants. It's also very likely that a major exchange launching a new venue would want to choose something with high throughput capacity and speed to handle the volume it could bring to the table.

Since its latest upgrade, Alpenglow, Solana finalizes transactions on its network in about 150 to 400 milliseconds. Avalanche takes about two full seconds, and the XRPL takes several seconds. In terms of transaction costs, Solana's median fee is $0.0004, whereas Avalanche's is $0.01, and the XRPL's is $0.00001. At first glance, it looks as if both Solana and the XRPL were passed over in favor of a more expensive (and in Solana's case, much slower) solution here.

Solana is also already home to a large sum of tokenized asset trading activity. It hosted $583 million in tokenized stocks as of Nov. 13, more than triple Avalanche's $179 million; the XRPL doesn't host any of those assets. So while it makes sense that the XRPL isn't a good fit for NYSE's needs, Solana still looks like a stronger option than what they actually went with on paper.

The XRP Ledger supports permissioned decentralized exchanges (DEXs), which are trading venues built into its blockchain that can be configured to admit only specific accounts holding approved credentials. That's a gated venue on a shared ledger, while the NYSE wanted a ledger of its own. One explanation for the NYSE's selection of Avalanche is that, per Ava Labs, the exchange will run its own custom blockchain built with Avalanche's technology, rather than settling on Avalanche's public chain. That fits the access control requirement.

So, Solana's and the XRPL's advantages mainly apply to their public ledgers, whose tokenized asset bases, transaction costs, and speed rankings mean little to a business looking to run its own private blockchain.

Realistically, Avalanche clinching the NYSE deal was a major missed opportunity for Solana and, to a lesser extent, XRP. But Solana holders should not be too hung up on that, as Solana landed a smaller win the same day.

Formation Securities told regulators on Nov. 9 that it plans to launch a new tokenized stock venue of its own running on Solana's network in early 2027, specifically citing its speed, low costs, and its existing base of tokenized real-world assets — ownership rights of things like stocks and bonds converted into tradeable crypto. Its trades would post directly to Solana's public ledger, incurring standard fees.

In contrast, Avalanche's NYSE deal will likely offer its coinholders little directly. So Solana lost some prestige here more than it lost potential revenue. XRP, for its part, just got new evidence that, somewhat surprisingly, its network's native compliance tooling is not as appealing to the institutions it's courting as what its developers and its investors may have hoped.

More broadly, the risk here is that other exchanges will copy the NYSE's template, launching their own blockchain products within small, exclusive walled gardens rather than launching them on public blockchains. That could lead to more lost business and further diminish the institutional adoption thesis for buying Solana and XRP, among many other coins.

Still, don't sell Solana or XRP over this.

During the next few quarters, watch for new exchanges for tokenized assets to announce their plans to launch and their chosen crypto partners. If XRP doesn't net any of those deals, it will be a deeply bearish sign, and if Solana can't capture at least a couple more, it's an indication that its competitive environment is getting fiercer and harder to navigate successfully.

#3073. Cyberattack Targets iPhones, Crypto of Visitors to Major Websites

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Cybersecurity

Hackers tried to inject malware for people going to Ikea, CNN, Zoom and other popular sites.

If you visited Ikea, CNN, Zoom or several other popular websites on Monday, it might be wise to update your iPhone or iPad immediately. Cybercriminals tried to infect iPhones and steal cryptocurrency from people who went to those sites, Reuters reports.

The compromised websites include Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, Ikea, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock, according to cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme and his platform Report URI. Helme said bad actors used Optimizely, a website optimization company, in an attempt to serve up JavaScript malware to people visiting sites from 178 organizations.

Ikea said it was investigating to see if any customers or digital services had been impacted. Zoom said it disabled Optimizely across its production environments and had not identified any effect on customer data. Equifax also has stopped using Optimizely and said it has not identified any compromise to systems or data.

Helme told CNET that “most people who simply read a page are at low risk,” but there are other actions you should take if you did more than that. He said if you entered debit or credit card details on any of the affected sites (the full list is here), check transactions and statements and maybe even get a replacement card.

If you copied and pasted a crypto wallet address on a site, make sure the funds went to the intended recipient, Helme suggested. Also, log out of all sessions on the affected websites and change your password. Finally, update to the latest iOS and restart the device if you use an iPhone or iPad running iOS 18.6 or earlier.

Optimizely said that the criminal “exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation” — the website testing system that clients use — to add the malicious JavaScript. The company said it had fixed the vulnerability, removed the bad code and “taken steps to secure affected user accounts.”

Reuters reported that Salesforce, Equifax and HSBC said their sites had not been compromised by the incident. Reuters also said it could not determine how much theft had occurred in the attack.

Report URI said that more than $7,000 in crypto was stolen within several hours of the attack’s start.

Optimizely is a platform used by many websites to manage content, test new website designs and tailor product recommendations to various target audiences. Customers load JavaScript snippets, which include Optimizely code and customer experiments, onto their websites to optimize site performance.

The snippets also contain a Project JavaScript field, which consists of code written by customers. But on Monday, the cybercriminal injected malicious code into that Project JavaScript field. Because the rest of the snippet was untouched, the files were still served from a host that every affected site already trusted.

The cost of cybercrime is forecast to reach $12.2 trillion by 2031, according to one estimate, an annual increase of 2.5% from 2026. That amount includes “stolen funds, fraud, productivity loss, intellectual property theft, post-attack remediation, regulatory fines and reputational harm.”

The Optimizely incident, dubbed the OptimJack attack, was the latest in a series of internet incidents around the globe. On Thursday, Microsoft’s Outlook email system went down, and the FAA grounded all planes on Friday. Microsoft blamed a software bug from July, and the FAA blamed a router.

Then, on Monday, Chase reported service disruptions and transaction delays, as did some Apple services on Tuesday.

None of these incidents were connected, Helme told CNET.

Testing Nvidia’s RTX Spark inside laptops for the past month felt like the birth of a different species of computer. Confined to a portable chassis, that local AI prowess and raw horsepower make good sense to turn it into a real everything machine.

But when you rip that N1X out of a laptop, drop it into a desk-bound mini PC like the Asus ProArt GR1X, and slap a price tag of at least $4,499 on it ($6,999 for the 128GB version I’m testing), the entire narrative changes.

Yes, when tethered to a wall, it is faster than its laptop counterpart. But this chip is no longer fighting the MacBook Pro. It is fighting the desktop market — a more ruthlessly powerful space where (in some ways) Nvidia is fighting with itself.

I currently have two 128GB heavyweights on the test bench. In the green corner is the Asus ProArt GR1X, powered by RTX Spark and 128GB of memory. In the red corner is the Geekom A9 Mega, armed with AMD’s Ryzen AI Max 395 and the exact same 128GB memory pool, but priced $3,000 cheaper.

And remember when I said Nvidia is fighting with itself in the desktop space? Well, to prove that point, I also threw my custom-built RTX 5070 Ti desktop into the ring for good measure (a quick foray on PC Part Picker shows that would be around $4,000 cheaper).

You are buying a 128GB mini PC to act as an always-on, hyper-secure household brain that you don’t pay subscriptions for. You want it to run a local model like Qwen 3.8 Flash via Hermes to autonomously organize your morning emails, scrape the web for news, or bridge with Home Assistant to tell your robot vacuum to clean the kitchen.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Measuring this comes down to two things: Tokens Per Second (TPS), which is how fast the AI types, and Time to First Token (TTFT), which is its reaction time before answering.

I pushed both machines through LM Studio using the Qwen 3.8 27B model on two standard generative tasks and one agentic task.

Nvidia’s chip has the reflexes of a driver hitting the apex at Silverstone. That sub-second reaction time makes conversational agents feel incredibly lifelike, and when I turned it into a self-hosted agent that I could talk to from my Telegram app, the end result was something that did the boring morning admin for me while I spoke to my wife on the phone instead.

Plus if you tap into Nvidia PAIR, you can use all the supported devices in your home to share AI compute. For example, a prompt on my MacBook Pro fired up the Spark machine for a longer task, while whirring my RTX 5070 Ti desktop into life for a short burst.

Meanwhile, the AMD machine is perfectly capable of this too, but it pauses just long enough for you to notice it clearing its throat. That being said, 24 tokens per second on Geekom is still faster than any human can read.

And as for the desktop PC, this is technically possible but with some caveats (because it treats all your system memory as different pools rather than one giant unified ocean):

That gaming rig is a Ferrari driving on a 100-foot track — unbelievably fast, but the track (its VRAM) is so short that you can only go so fast before crashing into the wall. The 128GB mini-PCs are freight trains with a lower top speed, but enough space to carry massive cargo (huge models) without ever derailing.

My custom RTX 5070 Ti desktop will absolutely smoke these mini PCs in standard graphical tasks. It’s a monster card that consumes more than double the total wattage of the RTX Spark (paying my respects to your electric bill and fan noise compared to the Spark).

But as I mentioned above, standard GPUs are fundamentally bottlenecked by their memory. It may be fast, but it only has the surface area of an airplane tray table. The moment you try to render high-res AI video or compile massive 3D Gaussian splats, the PC runs out of room.

The massive unified memory pool of RTX Spark gives you the surface area of a massive dining room table, swallowing heavy generative workloads whole.

I booted up ComfyUI for local video generation and ran the synthetic Procyon benchmarking suite to measure raw compute overhead.

This is an absolute bloodbath. Nvidia’s proprietary Tensor cores and hyper-efficient NVFP4 precision formats completely lap AMD’s Strix Halo. As you can see, Spark generated the exact same ComfyUI video nearly three times faster.

If you are a 3D artist, indie game developer or an ad agency director generating local video assets on a tight deadline, rendering time is literally money. In those professional environments, the Asus ProArt GR1X pays for itself.

Though, quick side note Asus. This is a creator machine — would it have killed you to put an SD card reader on here? For moving photos, I've gotta head back into dongle hell.

But for everyday people like you and me? It comes down to how you feel about all this stuff. Personally, there’s a big difference in my mind between human creativity and getting a typed prompt right to churn out AI stuff.

And while there are improvements on that human side — Adobe Creative Suite is now optimized for RTX Spark, for example — I didn’t really use it for anything beyond my YouTube video intro and some fun experiments with my wife’s doodles.

You’re paying a massive premium for AI, so it might as well play video games well, too, at the end of the day. I mean, that’s a lot of money — you want this to be a true everything machine.

I ran all the usual 3DMark benchmarks to measure raw, unassisted graphics muscle, and checked the frame rates on key games before and after DLSS.

Black Myth Wukong (1440p Cinematic NO DLSS)

Cyberpunk 2077 (1440p Ray Tracing Ultra NO DLSS)

Cyberpunk 2077 (1440p Ray Tracing Ultra DLSS 4.5 Balanced w/ Dynamic Frame Gen)

In use, it’s nice to have a mini PC that’s capable of gaming in the way that it is. But in the desktop space, this is RTX Spark’s harshest reality check. If gaming is something you care about chiefly over getting stuff done, you know, I know (and Nvidia knows) you should get a gaming PC.

Not to say it doesn’t work brilliantly, because it does. This is a mighty integrated GPU that does smoke AMD, keeping the machine nicely viable for high-end 1440p gaming with all the DLSS support.

But a standard RTX 5070 Ti desktop, which you could easily build (or buy) for half the price of the Asus, doubles the Spark’s native performance.

RTX Spark mini PCs, such as the Asus ProArt GR1X, are localized token generators disguised as PCs. It’s not going to be for everyone, so let me help you out here.

RTX Spark is a cheat code. Its power impresses, and the speed gains mean you won’t be spending time twiddling your thumbs waiting for it. And the RTX side of it for gaming makes this a machine you can work on by day and play by night.

AMD power does 80% of what the Nvidia box can do in daily tasks, and it leaves you with a lot more money in your pocket. Of course there’s a speed advantage with Spark, but is it $3,000 of an advantage? That’s up to you.

If you’ve got the space for an actual desktop, this is going to be the move. Component prices are steep, but even with that in mind, you’ll get better bang for your buck in gaming and short burst AI/creativity work.

#3071. I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes – it was satisfying

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

A new Gemini Notebook feature lets you create interactive sites from intricate data.

Google’s Gemini can now turn your notes and other sources in your Gemini Notebook (previously called NotebookLM) into interactive pages or sites to help you better process complicated information.

Complete with flashcards, dashboards, and colorful panels, the sites make it easier to study and understand intricate concepts. I tested the feature, announced Tuesday, to see how efficient it is at creating a navigable site that is actually helpful and stays loyal to sources.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector in my tests

Because Notebooks are built with the sources you provide, like textbooks, files, or notes, the sites are created with the data that is in your Gemini Notebook. Notebook has three tabs: Sources, Chat, and Studio. The site option is in the Studio tab, listed under what you can create.

If you’re taking a college class, you could put all the information you need to prepare for a test and use the interactive site as a study guide that you can share with others.

To test this, I gave Notebook the following prompt:

“Make me a site that visually explains how cellular respiration works, breaking down each stage with interactive diagrams and self-check flashcards.”

Since I’m not in a class that would give me those study materials, I gave Gemini online sources to use for this. #3070. Celsius vs. Hershey: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Energy drinks or candy bars? We put a high-growth upstart up against a 130-year-old sweets empire.

By Josh Kohn-Lindquist – Updated Nov 18, 2026 at 6:59AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Celsius Holdings ›

Choosing between growth and stability often defines an investment strategy. You might consider whether the rapid expansion of Celsius (CELH +6.38%) or the enduring legacy of Hershey (HSY +1.46%) is the better buy.

Celsius represents the high-growth side of the beverage market, focusing on functional energy drinks that appeal to health-conscious consumers. Hershey remains a cornerstone of the confectionery world, offering massive scale and predictable returns through its dominant position in chocolate and snacks.

Celsius focuses on the functional beverage market, selling energy drinks designed to boost metabolism and provide sustained energy. It reaches consumers through major retailers and e-commerce platforms like Amazon (AMZN +1.98%), while competing among beverage stocks for shelf space. A critical component of its strategy is a distribution agreement with Pepsi, which provides the necessary infrastructure to scale quickly. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as Pepsi accounted for roughly 43.2% of revenue recently.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $3.2 billion. This figure represents revenue growth of approximately 49.1% compared to the prior twelve-month period. During the same window, the company reported net income of nearly $230.2 million, demonstrating its ability to maintain profitability as it scales its footprint across North America and international markets.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.2x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity, indicating how much the company relies on borrowing to fund its operations. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term liabilities with current assets, is roughly 1.7x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $72.1 million. Free cash flow represents the cash a company generates after accounting for cash outflows to support operations and maintain its capital assets.

Hershey operates as a global leader in the confectionery and snacking industry, producing well-known brands ranging from chocolate bars to protein snacks. The company sells its products through wholesale distributors and major retail chains, with McLane Company, Inc. serving as its largest customer, accounting for approximately 27% of net sales. This customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business, though Hershey offsets this with a presence in over 65 countries. Its strategy emphasizes brand loyalty and consistent product innovation to maintain its market-leading position.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 27, 2026, revenue reached close to $12.3 billion. This reflects revenue growth of approximately 6.7% over the previous year, showing steady progress in a mature market. The company reported net income of nearly $1.8 billion during this period, highlighting the strong cash-generating power of its established brand portfolio.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.2x. The current ratio is approximately 1.2x, suggesting the company maintains sufficient liquidity to meet its immediate financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $1.8 billion. This robust cash generation allows the company to support its operations and return value to shareholders through various capital allocation strategies.

Celsius faces significant revenue concentration with Pepsi, creating a high level of dependency on a single partner for distribution. The company also faces intense competition from global brands like Monster Beverage (MNST +1.47%) and Coca-Cola (KO -1.04%). Operational risks include a reliance on third-party co-packers and potential supply chain disruptions for aluminum cans and specific ingredients. Furthermore, the integration of new brands like Alani Nu could lead to operational challenges or cannibalize its existing product lines.

Hershey faces significant commodity price volatility, especially in cocoa and sugar, which can affect its gross margin. The company must also manage the risk of sales volume declines if price increases intended to offset rising input costs lead to consumer pushback. Competition from global giants like Nestlé (NSRGF -3.36%) remains a constant pressure, requiring continuous marketing and innovation. Additionally, Hershey faces complexities in international operations and potential cybersecurity threats that could disrupt its global supply chain.

Celsius trades at a slightly higher earnings multiple than Hershey, though its lower price-to-sales ratio might appeal to those prioritizing rapid revenue expansion.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

The Forward P/E provides a look at the stock price relative to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures the market value against sales over the past twelve months.

While Celsius certainly offers the more exciting growth profile versus steady-Eddie Hershey, its organic sales growth likely lies closer to the high single digits as of its most recent quarter. Celsius's skyrocketing revenue in 2026 primarily came from adding Alani Nu to its operations via its $1.8 billion acquisition of the up-and-coming energy drink maker, rather than true organic sales growth.

That said, Alani Nu rapidly surpassed the company's namesake Celsius brand as its best-selling drink -- and its growth isn't slowing yet. Alani Nu grew revenue by 24% (product sold to distributors) and saw retail sales rise 58% (product sold at c-stores, or grocery stores, for example), highlighting the brand's growing popularity. On top of Alani Nu's success, Celsius grew international revenue by 78%, and these foreign sales account for just 5% of the company's total revenue, leaving a potentially decades-long growth runway ahead.

With a portfolio of Alani Nu, Celsius, Rockstar, and international sales, Celsius should provide reasonable growth upside over the foreseeable future -- just don't expect 2026's growth rates to repeat, barring another major acquisition.

Hershey, meanwhile, is a stalwart chocolatier and snacking behemoth paying a well-funded and growing dividend that yields 3.3%. The company's days of consistent double-digit sales growth are behind it, but management expects adjusted EPS to rise by roughly 7% annually over the long term. Leaning on its strategy as a serial acquirer, I fully expect Hershey to meet this goal as it builds out its steadily growing salty snacks portfolio (primarily popcorn and pretzels). GLP-1 medications certainly pose a threat to Hershey's business, but I believe the peptide may, counterintuitively, be a benefit to the company, as miniaturization and smaller packaging could boost margins.

Ultimately, I'm not in a rush to buy more shares of either stock, though I do own both. However, I would lean toward buying Celsius in 2027, given its stronger growth potential and similar valuation to Hershey. Investors seeking stability and passive income may be better off buying Hershey, though, so it comes down to any individual investor's goals and risk appetite.

#3069. Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

You’ll soon be able to turn off Gemini model training but still retain access to your previous chats with Google’s AI.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me

In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Currently, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google said in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both new settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”

#3068. SpaceX Misses Its Double Catch but Still Makes History by Catching the Starship

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The Super Heavy V3 booster fell into the Gulf of Mexico, where it was later recovered

SpaceX came up short on an ambitious double-catch attempt during Friday’s Launch 15, snagging only one of the two rockets it aimed to recover. The company hoped to capture both the Starship spacecraft and the Super Heavy V3 booster, building on a maneuver it first pulled off with a single booster just over two years ago and has since repeated multiple times.

SpaceX’s Launch 15 lifted off cleanly Friday evening, reaching orbit to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before the stages returned to Earth. Back in Boca Chica, Texas, ground crews aimed to snag the upgraded Super Heavy V3 booster using Mechazilla, SpaceX’s towering launch-and-catch structure. While the company had previously caught its older V1 booster three times, Friday’s flight marked its first attempt to recover the V3 variant.

That recovery attempt fell short. SpaceX is still investigating the cause, though spokesperson Kate Tice noted during Friday’s webcast that the booster “ended its boostback (burn) early due to a low fuel mass alarm.” The premature shutdown forced the Super Heavy V3 to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico, where recovery crews later retrieved it.

Meanwhile, the upper-stage Starship pressed on, deploying its satellites and completing roughly 14 orbits before reentering on Saturday. Nearly 24 hours after liftoff, SpaceX successfully caught the returning spacecraft with Mechazilla.

“Starship navigated its way back to the east coast of Texas, flew a final swoosh maneuver out over the Gulf, and approached the same launch site it had just left 22.5 hours prior,” SpaceX said in a statement. “After breaking through the clouds, three Raptor engines ignited for a landing flip and slow descent into Mechazilla’s waiting arms, which closed to catch Starship for the very first time.”

The initial goal was to catch both the Super Heavy V3 booster and the Starship itself, a feat that SpaceX had not attempted before. It also would’ve been the first time in human history that a space company caught both its booster rocket and the upper stage, which would’ve scored a big win for rocket reusability.

SpaceX was unable to secure the Super Heavy V3 booster, but it was still able to catch the Starship. Despite missing the dual catch, the operation represents a significant engineering milestone, as it is the first time SpaceX has successfully caught a rocket’s upper stage after launch.

SpaceX streamed the flight from its X account and the company’s website. You can watch the entire webcast on X. It lasts approximately 23.5 hours and covers the launch, the Super Heavy V3 crash into the Gulf of Mexico and the eventual catch of the Starship.

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The Chrome update includes more useful vertical tabs, easier screen sharing, and some handy keyboard shortcuts.

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 update for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of new features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

Also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android users is something else

Here are the five new Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

If you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome update adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly

When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

This auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

The Chrome update allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a new window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.)

The system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

Also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast

Outside of these new features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the new features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually update by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with new Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising

If the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the update, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.
